### DW-242: Zero-damage units are locked out of Patrol/Follow/AttackBuilding by the pre-switch combat gate
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-1.12 (2026-06-25)" + "Deferred from: code review of story-2.9a (2026-07-01)" item 1 — merged), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:121-126
severity: medium
reason: The `EffectiveAttackDamage == 0 → continue` gate still sits above the whole command switch (which now also carries AttackBuilding/PickupItem/Patrol/Follow), so zero-damage non-gatherers sit inert in those commands with no normalize-to-Idle. Fix = hoist pure-movement branches above the gate TOGETHER WITH DW-202's wave filter (else zero-damage units start auto-attacking). Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle noncombatant-command-gate - CombatSystem.cs:126's pre-switch `EffectiveAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero -> continue` blanket skip now routes through a new movement-only TickNonCombatant instead of skipping the entity, exactly the one-gate-hoist this entry prescribes. AttackMove and Patrol run their movement half only (ResumeAttackMove/ResumePatrol - AttackMove's arrival normalize-to-Idle is what also closes DW-202's pool leak at the combat end); Follow reuses TickFollowCombat verbatim because it is pure tracking for every unit; AttackTarget and AttackBuilding normalize to Idle with both target refs and both flags cleared, the same disposal the gatherer guard directly above applies to the same orders (this entry's reason line names no-normalize-to-Idle as the defect). Every acquisition/engagement path stays CLOSED to non-combatants - deliberately, since this entry warns that hoisting engagement would make zero-damage units auto-attack. Determinism: all 25 goldens byte-unchanged because every resting state (Idle/Move/Stop/HoldPosition/Build/PickupItem) stays a no-op byte-identical to the old blanket skip; every golden scenario carrying a zero-damage unit (FormationSeparation, CommandVocabulary, MultiFaction, MergedTickN2, MidMatchDrop) was audited and all sit in Idle or Move. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4860/0/1, 16 of the 18 new tests proven RED against the run-base - the 2 that pass in both states are deliberate fences (a non-combatant at Idle or under Move must stay completely untouched, so a future edit that routes movement can never quietly start routing engagement). Residual filed separately as DW-643: the zero-damage predicate is spelled `== Fixed.Zero` here and `> Fixed.Zero` in the AI, complements only by ModifierSystem's clamp, which SaveGameState's restore path bypasses.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle noncombatant-command-gate (Epic 15, Story 15.4)

### DW-249: SearchArea over-cap selection is cell-ordered, not global lowest-ID
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: story 2.1 (2026-06-25)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/SearchAreaEffect.cs:51-64; godot/src/Navigation/SpatialHash.cs:179
severity: medium
reason: Unchanged — QueryRadius has no filter/priority parameter; the caveat comment survives verbatim. Deterministic but not the documented contract. One SpatialHash API change closes this + DW-250. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: resolved by sweep bundle dw-searcharea-target-selection-correctness — New godot/src/Navigation/IEntityQueryFilter.cs + SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter>: when the buffer is full the largest RETAINED id is evicted rather than the late-scanned candidate being dropped, so the kept set is the globally lowest-N over the whole radius and the written prefix comes out ascending — the contract the class doc always claimed. SearchAreaEffect.FindTargets consumes it and no longer Array.Sorts. TFilter is struct-constrained so the per-candidate test is devirtualized with no delegate and no boxing, preserving the zero-alloc contract. The unfiltered QueryRadius is left byte-identical on purpose: MovementSystem's separation pass uses it and its output feeds Position, a SimChecksum input — that half is DW-512. No cap constant changed (RulesetHash untouched); no golden moved or was re-recorded.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle searcharea-target-selection-correctness (Epic 15, Story 15.4)

## Deferred from: code review of story-2.1 (2026-06-25) — migrated 2026-07-28

### DW-250: SearchArea truncates the hit buffer BEFORE the faction filter — enemy fan-out under-selects
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-2.1 (2026-06-25)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/SearchAreaEffect.cs:64-78
severity: medium
reason: Unchanged — 64-slot buffer fills unfiltered, sorts, THEN compacts by TargetMatcher; the recommended pass-filter-into-QueryRadius fix has not happened. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: resolved by sweep bundle dw-searcharea-target-selection-correctness — Root cause was ordering: the 64-slot buffer filled via the UNFILTERED QueryRadius, sorted, then compacted by TargetMatcher, so non-matching entities consumed slots before the filter ran (an Enemy-filtered nuke cast amid 64+ of the caster's own allies selected ZERO enemies while enemies stood in the radius). Fixed by evaluating the predicate BEFORE a candidate may occupy a slot, via the new SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter>; the predicate is still the single TargetMatcher.Matches, wrapped as the new nested TargetMatcher.QueryFilter so no consumption site can drift. Proven RED without the fix (EnemyFanOut_IsNotStarved_ByACrowdOfLowerIdAllies and OverCap_MatchingEnemies_StillFillTheWholeFanOut_WhenAlliesCrowdTheRadius both fail on the pre-fix body).
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle searcharea-target-selection-correctness (Epic 15, Story 15.4)

### DW-266: StatusFlags are authorable and hashed but read by NOTHING — authored stuns are silent no-ops
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: story 2.2b (2026-06-26)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs; godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs; godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs
severity: critical
reason: HEADLINE GAP — StatusFlagsOf is written/folded (EntityWorld, ModifierStore, SimChecksum) but whole-repo grep shows zero reads in CombatSystem/MovementSystem/AbilityCastSystem, while all five flags (Disarmed/Stunned/Rooted/Silenced/Invulnerable) are authorable through the 2.5 editor and JSON. An authored stun costs energy, shows in the HUD, and does nothing. Determinism-relevant fix (golden re-baseline). Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: Bundle status-flags-become-real (workflow burn-down 2026-08-04) — verified still open (written/folded/authorable/rendered, read by ZERO runtime consumers), then implemented exactly the recorded 2026-07-28 routing below. Stunned → a whole-unit gate at the top of CombatSystem.Tick (no cooldown tick, acquire, chase, attack or on-hit rider; drops AttackTarget, clears Attacking) + the MovementSystem anchor + the AbilityCastSystem refusal; Rooted → the MovementSystem anchor, exempt from seek AND separation (mirroring the Story 1.12 HoldPosition anchor) so neither its own order nor a neighbour shove displaces it; Disarmed → both CombatSystem damage choke points (TryDealDamage + TryDealBuildingDamage), checked BEFORE the cooldown is consumed so a disarm burns no attack timer and spawns no projectile; Silenced → an atomic TryCast refusal (nothing debited, no cooldown, no graph run) with a new DenialReason; Invulnerable → DamageResolver.Apply, the single entity-damage path covering melee hitscan, projectile primary + splash and every DamageEffect leaf. Every gate is a PAUSE not a cancel (CommandState/MoveTarget/Moving untouched) so the order resumes the tick the modifier expires. Two new DenialReason members (Silenced, Stunned) + DenialReasonText mappings. Determinism: no golden moved or was re-recorded — StatusFlagsOf is None for every entity in every recorded golden scenario, so no new branch is ever entered. CONTENT LANDMINE FIXED: godot/resources/data/abilities/aura_guard.json authored `"status": "Stunned"` on an Ally-filtered +5-armor aura — a no-op while the flag was unread, a permanent mass-stun of your own army the instant it became real; set to "None". Coverage: 13 tests in StatusFlagRuntimeTests.cs including an end-to-end authored-modifier install/expire (no test shortcut writes StatusFlagsOf); negative control against f93e678 fails 12 of 13, the 13th being the None no-op control that must pass on both sides. Gates: dotnet build 0 errors; Tier-1 4855/0/1 (baseline 4842 + 13 new), no flake.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — Story 15.3 (status effects become real): Disarmed→CombatSystem gate, Rooted/Stunned→MovementSystem+combat, Silenced→AbilityCastSystem refuse, Invulnerable→DamageResolver

### DW-283: Ability cost debits discard return values — negative CostEnergy would partial-spend
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("From code review of story-2.4a (2026-06-28)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs:193,215-217,240-252
severity: medium
reason: Unchanged, and the check-then-debit surface GREW: a 4th cost (CostHealth, debited after the graph) now relies on the same pre-check/debit lockstep; TryDebitEnergy returns false without mutating on cost<0 while the pre-check passes negatives. Gated only by the authoring validator today. Cheap fail-closed asserts on the debit returns. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle ability-cast-path-hardening - verified still-open at AbilityCastSystem.cs:241-243 (all three cost debits discarded their return values). Root cause characterised: the affordability pre-checks are `have >= cost` comparisons that a NEGATIVE authored cost passes trivially, while the debits DISAGREE about it - ModifierStore.TryDebitEnergy refuses cost<0 without mutating, but ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal subtract a negative and therefore GRANT resources, so a negative-cost ability printed ore/crystal, ran its effect graph and started its cooldown while its energy price silently never applied. Fix = a fail-closed negative-cost gate (energy/ore/crystal/health) BEFORE any mutation, plus checked + short-circuited debits that roll back exactly what landed on an unexpected refusal (AC6 refuse-atomic); the rollback arm is the documented fail-closed backstop and the gate is what makes it unreachable for validator-clean content. Determinism: CombatEventQueue is not a SimChecksum input and the gate/rollback are unreachable for clean content; no golden moved or was re-recorded. Covered by rows in the bundle's 24 new Tier-1 tests (godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Effects/AbilityCastPathHardeningTests.cs), proven RED by temporarily reverting the gate + checked debits in place (6 failures together with the DW-284 validator revert), then restored and re-verified. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4866/0/1 run twice (baseline 4842 + 24), no flake. Residual filed separately as DW-642: ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal still CREDIT on a negative cost for every OTHER caller (BuildingSystem, BuyItemCommand, ReviveHeroCommand, AiOpponentSystem) - the systemic primitive-level fix is out of this entry's scope.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle ability-cast-path-hardening (Epic 15, Story 15.9)

### DW-284: SecondsToTicks 16.16 overflow for cooldowns above ~1092s — no validator upper bound
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("From code review of story-2.4a (2026-06-28)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs:81,255; godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs:81-82
severity: low
reason: Unchanged — conversion unclamped, validator has only the lower bound. ScenarioDirector guards its own conversion with Math.Max(1, ...) — precedent for the one-line fix + validator upper bound. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle ability-cast-path-hardening - verified still-open at AbilityCastSystem.cs:81 + AbilityValidator.cs:93-94. SecondsToTicks multiplied through Fixed.operator*, whose 16.16 product is cast back to int32, so any cooldown above ~1092.27 s wrapped to a NEGATIVE tick count - which the `> 0` countdown gate reads as ready, i.e. the longest authorable cooldown became NO cooldown at all (measured: 2000 s -> -5536 ticks). Fix = a 64-bit intermediate (`(long)seconds.Raw * TicksPerSecond >> 16`), algebraically identical below the bound, plus the missing validator UPPER bound referencing the new public AbilityCastSystem.MaxCooldownSeconds (raw int.MaxValue/TICKS_PER_SECOND) rather than a hand-copied number (DW-125 lesson). Determinism: AbilityCooldownTicks is folded (SimChecksum v7), so byte-identity below the bound is pinned by an explicit test over 0/3/6/10/12/15/20 s, the sub-tick 0.01 s case and the boundary value itself; all shipped ability cooldowns are 0-20 s. No golden moved and none was re-recorded. Proven RED by reverting SecondsToTicks in place (1 failure) and the validator bound (part of the 6-failure revert), both then restored and re-verified. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4866/0/1 run twice.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle ability-cast-path-hardening (Epic 15, Story 15.9)

### DW-304: OrderApplier building commands no-op silently when BuildingSystem is null
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-2.8 (2026-07-01)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/NetworkCommand.cs:208-216
severity: low
reason: Unchanged and the surface GREW — the null-elvis pattern spread from Train to SetRally (and the Revive/Research family): an accidental null wiring is a deterministic silent no-op indistinguishable from intentional headless-null. Unreachable today (wiring unconditional in MatchLifecycleController). Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: done via bundle lockstep-wiring-fail-loud (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-03) - Verified still real first (the null-elvis surface had grown to 7 commands: Train/CancelTrain/SetRally/ReviveHero/BuyItem via `buildings`, StartResearch/CancelResearch via `research`). OrderApplier.Apply gained an optional injected ILogSink tail parameter - the codebase's AR-4 logging seam, whose docs forbid Console and static ambient sinks, and whose existing OrderApplier_Train_NullBuildings_IsDeterministicNoOp / CancelTrain_NullBuildings_IsDeterministicNoOp tests lock the no-throw contract, so "fail loud" here = Warn through the injected sink, not assert/throw. Each building-family branch now warns once, naming the dropped command, wire id, faction, and the missing system, then performs the exact same deterministic no-op: zero sim-state or SimChecksum-input change, zero golden movement. The sink is threaded through the Godot-free production paths (MergedTickApplier forwards it; ReplayPlayer gained a Log field) and the Godot-coupled LockstepManager passes a Log field defaulted to GodotLogSink (LoopbackDesyncSelfTest precedent), so the live online/offline lockstep paths scream with no per-match wiring - surviving exactly the wiring drift this entry describes. 17 new Godot-free OrderApplierFailLoudTests pin warn-once-per-command naming command+system, wired-system silence on both success and guard rejects, sink-less legacy silence/no-throw, and the MergedTickApplier + ReplayPlayer forwarding. Gate: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj 0 errors; full Tier-1 suite 4128 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle lockstep-wiring-fail-loud (Epic 15, Story 15.7)

### DW-464: The ONLINE concede path has two unpolished robustness/UX gaps — (a) `LockstepManager.EnqueueConcede`'s online…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-2-in-match-menu-pause-game-speed-concede-surrender-leave-victory-defeat-score-screen.md`
reason: The ONLINE concede path has two unpolished robustness/UX gaps — (a) `LockstepManager.EnqueueConcede`'s online branch silently drops the concede order when `_pendingCount >= TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS` (returns false, `MainScene.IssueConcede` ignores it, no retry/feedback), and (b) after a confirmed online concede the menu closes immediately with no "surrendering…" feedback while the verdict only latches a tick-round-trip later, so the player is dropped back into a still-live match as if nothing happened. — Evidence: Surfaced by the Story 11.2 adversarial + edge-case review. Both are online-only: the offline path applies the concede immediately (verified in the in-engine gate — P1→LOST resolves next tick), so neither is reachable in the currently-shippable offline skirmish. Live MP is explicitly deferred to Epic 9 (the spec scopes online as "not in-engine verifiable now"), so these are genuine but un-exercisable now. Fix when the MP shell lands: buffer/retry a dropped concede (a rare high-intent order must not be lost on a busy tick) and give the online player pending-surrender feedback (disable Concede / show "Surrendering…") until the verdict latches.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: `concede-buffer-retry` bundle (e959dd0) — both halves fixed. (a) New Godot-free `ConcedeBuffer` (godot/src/Multiplayer/ConcedeBuffer.cs, single-file-included in SimSources.props per the DelayMath/HandshakeGate precedent): EnqueueConcede latches a sticky queued flag, Flush's send branch claims a batch slot for it (retrying next send on a full batch), and EnqueueOrder/EnqueueDslEvent reserve the last slot while one is queued so order spam can never starve it; reset on GoOnline/GoSpectate/GoOffline. (b) `InMatchMenuOverlay.SetSurrenderPending` keeps the menu OPEN with Concede disabled and relabeled "Surrendering…", driven by MainScene.IssueConcede from the real EnqueueConcede result (guarded so a spectator's no-op press shows no false promise) and cleared at the three verdict/reset seams. Offline flow unchanged; all changes client-send-side or presentation-only, nothing folded into SimChecksum, zero goldens moved; Tier-1 4118/0/1. Spectator enabled-Concede quirk filed as DW-612; live two-client verification owed via DW-613.

### DW-466: SP saves are not portable across machines and the format cannot detect it; make AiOpponentSystem Fixed-point (or…

### DW-469: The 256-entry `CombatEventQueue` ring silently drops events when full, and denial/completion cues now share that…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
reason: The 256-entry `CombatEventQueue` ring silently drops events when full, and denial/completion cues now share that lossy queue with no priority — a large single-tick battle (>256 hit pushes) can drop a denial or training-complete cue. — Evidence: `CombatEventQueue.MAX_EVENTS=256` with silent drop-when-full (pre-existing); 11.4 adds `OrderDenied`/`TrainingComplete`/`ResearchComplete` consumption to the same queue. Reserving headroom or prioritising non-hit events is a queue-design change beyond this story's scope; self-healing and low-likelihood.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: Bundle combat-event-queue-capacity (workflow burn-down 2026-08-04) — verified still open against current code, then fixed. Two-lane admission behind a single private `HasRoomFor(type)` gate both `Push` overloads and `PushDenied` route through: `MAX_AMBIENT_EVENTS = 256` (the old flat capacity, so battle-cue admission and drain-side worst case are unchanged) + `PRIORITY_RESERVE = 64` slots only low-volume notification cues can occupy, `MAX_EVENTS = 320`; `public static bool IsAmbient(CombatEventType)` is a closed list of spammy types with a fail-safe default (a new enum member is treated as a notification, over-protecting rather than starving a cue). Deliberately NOT a 4x ring: growing it multiplies per-frame drain work in exactly the huge-battle frame where budget is tightest, for zero perceptible gain. Determinism: no golden/checksum/replay can move — every `.Count`/`.Get(` read resolves only in AudioManager/CombatFeedbackBridge/MatchAlertBridge, no sim system reads the queue and SimChecksum references it only in comments; no new instance fields so the StoreClearCompleteness fixture needed no change. Mutant-verified: reverting `HasRoomFor` to the lane-blind `_count < MAX_EVENTS` fails 8 of the 26 new tests including DenialRaisedDuringABattleFlood_IsStillAdmittedWithItsReason. Gates: dotnet build 0 errors (11 pre-existing warnings); Tier-1 4868/0/1 (baseline 4842 + exactly 26 new); a repeat run produced only the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf flake, which passed 2/2 in isolation.

### DW-476: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `SelectionSystem.ConfirmOrder` acked unconditionally, so a Shift-queued order onto full…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
location: SelectionSystem.cs:634
reason: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `SelectionSystem.ConfirmOrder` acked unconditionally, so a Shift-queued order onto full order rings produced the confirmation AND the `QueueFull` refusal for one click. — Evidence: Found by the post-merge ultra-review (2026-07-29), `SelectionSystem.cs:634`. Note the issue-time-optimism itself is the deliberate GDD §6 design (and was rejected as a finding during 11.4's own review); the defect is only the contradictory DOUBLE feedback on the one guard that rejects synchronously at issue time. Cheapest fix: suppress the ack when the local ring-full precheck already knows the order cannot be queued.
status: resolved
resolution: `ConfirmOrder` takes a `queued` flag and, when set, acks only if some selected unit still has ring room — reading the same FOLDED `OrderQueueCount` the guard rejects on, so the two cannot disagree. Threaded through the four queued-capable issue paths (move, attack-move, attack-target, attack-building). Issue-time optimism is retained everywhere else; this covers only the guard that rejects synchronously at issue time.

### DW-477: **RESOLVED 2026-07-29** — Alt+LMB on the minimap dropped a ping AND panned the camera to the pinged point
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
location: MinimapBridge.cs:248
reason: **RESOLVED 2026-07-29** — Alt+LMB on the minimap dropped a ping AND panned the camera to the pinged point. — Evidence: Found by the post-merge ultra-review (2026-07-29), `MinimapBridge.cs:248`, then CONFIRMED IN-ENGINE the same day: an Alt+LMB at minimap px (1750, 1030) moved the camera pivot to `(-79.36, 0, 74.24)`, the exact world point clicked. Root cause was wider than first described: the Alt branch consumed only the PRESS, so BOTH the matching release (the pan branch never tested `mb.Pressed`) and any drag leaked through. FIXED by a `_pingGesture` latch that swallows the remainder of the gesture, self-healing on a plain press so a release delivered outside the Control cannot strand it. Re-verified in-engine: Alt+click and Alt+drag both leave the pivot at `(0,0,0)`; a plain click still pans to `(-79.36, 0, 74.24)`.
status: resolved

### DW-478: Depth-5 production queue lets a player queue N units against unchanged live SupplyUsed (supply is consumed at…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-6-production-queue-depth-5-with-queue-display-and-cancel-refund.md`
location: godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs:422-427
reason: Depth-5 production queue lets a player queue N units against unchanged live SupplyUsed (supply is consumed at spawn, never reserved at enqueue), so queuing can overshoot the supply cap by up to 4. — Evidence: BuildingSystem.TrainUnit (godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs:422-427) gates each enqueue with resources.HasSupply against SupplyUsed, which is recomputed from LIVE units and never incremented by enqueue; five enqueues therefore all see the same headroom. At depth-1 (2.8) at most one order was ever in flight so overshoot was impossible — the depth-5 widening (this story) introduces it. Deferred, not fixed: reserving supply on enqueue (WC3-strict) vs consume-at-spawn (the existing model, kept deliberately) is a design decision the intent does not specify; consequence is a self-correcting balance overshoot (own-ore overspend, deterministic across peers), not a crash/desync/free-resource exploit.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle production-queue-correctness) - BuildingSystem.TrainUnit now gates on HasSupply(faction, cost + QueuedSupply(faction)) - a gate-time projection re-derived from the already-folded production queue, never written into the checksum-folded SupplyUsed. Per the recorded 2026-07-30 WC3-strict decision.
decision: 2026-07-30 Reserve supply at enqueue (WC3-strict) — Count queued supply against the cap to prevent overshoot

### DW-485: FlowFieldSystem._cache is an unbounded Dictionary — every distinct destination cell holds a ~200 KB field until the next building/terrain change
origin: filed from the Epic-11 retrospective (action item A8-E11) and the A5-E11 map-size verdict, 2026-07-30
source_spec: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/map-size-brainstorm-brief.md` (V2 prerequisite / V5 item 2)
location: godot/src/Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs (`_cache`, Dictionary<int, FlowField> keyed by goal cell)
severity: medium
reason: `FlowFieldSystem._cache` has no eviction limit — a field is computed on demand per unique goal cell and lives until `RebuildObstacles` / `SetBuildingObstacle` / `SetStaticBlocked` / `InvalidateCache` clears the whole dictionary, so ~100 distinct move orders between building events holds ~20 MB. — Evidence: read during the 2026-07-30 map-size verdict work; the cache is cleared only on obstacle/terrain change, never bounded by size or age, and nothing evicts a stale goal cell. Not a determinism risk (the cache is a pure function of the grid and is rebuilt identically on every peer) and not a per-tick cost — this is a retained-memory issue. Worth fixing on its own merits, and a HARD PREREQUISITE for map-size Route B (`GRID_SIZE` 128→256), which would multiply each entry to ~800 KB / ~80 MB at the same order count. Fix: an LRU or size cap on the dictionary. Filed as a numbered entry so a sweep can actually pick it up — the retro action item A8-E11 had no ledger entry and was therefore invisible to triage.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `flowfield-cache-bound` (commit 71b585d) - FlowFieldSystem._cache bounded at MAX_CACHED_FIELDS = 32 with deterministic monotonic-stamp LRU eviction routed through one ClearCache helper; evicted fields are never pooled so in-flight FlowFieldBridge references stay valid and an evicted field recomputes byte-identical; 6 new Godot-free tests, zero goldens moved.

### DW-488: ModifierSystem.AccumulateBonus's `+=` accumulator stays unsaturated after the DW-28 recompute clamp — a large POSITIVE +MaxHealth stack that wraps the accumulator negative now KILLS the over-buffed unit via the new DW-325 trigger
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:152-155 (AccumulateBonus `_flat*Bonus[id] += delta`, wrapping)
severity: medium
reason: DW-28 saturated the `Base + bonus` READ in `RecomputeEntity` but not the per-modifier accumulator write, so a stack of large +MaxHealth modifiers can wrap `_flatMaxHealthBonus` negative BEFORE the read; `AddSaturating(Base, wrappedNegative)` then saturates to `MinValue` → `Max(0,…)==0` → the new DW-325 trigger now KILLS the over-buffed unit (previously it was a benign 0-ceiling zombie), a strictly worse divergent outcome. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case + intent-alignment lenses independently landed on it; `AddSaturating`'s own docstring concedes "a widen-then-clamp cannot recover a value that has ALREADY wrapped in the int add." Not closable by saturating the accumulator itself — per-step saturation would break `AccumulateBonus`'s order-independence invariant at the boundary; DW-28's intent offered "or a Base+modifier authoring bound" as the alternative. Full closure = a content-authoring cap on `MaxStacks × delta` magnitude (a validator rule). Content-gated + requires an already-extreme base; deterministic (no desync).
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle modifier-robustness-and-ceiling) - Closed on the authoring side as the entry prescribes: Modifier.MaxStatDeltaTotalRaw (int.MaxValue / EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity) + Modifier.MaxAuthorableStacks, exposed as Modifier.CheckAuthoringBounds() and enforced fail-closed by AbilityValidator on every ApplyModifierEffect across all four stat deltas, making the 8-slot accumulator un-wrappable by construction. Not added to EffectCaps (would move RulesetHash).

### DW-489: ModifierStore.Apply / RemoveByModifierId gained a "target may be destroyed on return" post-condition (DW-325); external callers were not audited and cannot distinguish "installed & alive" from "installed & host died"
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`

severity: medium
reason: The DW-325 kill makes `Apply` and `RemoveByModifierId` able to `Destroy`+recycle the host, a post-condition they never had; only the 3 INTERNAL `ApplyStatDeltas` callers were guarded. `ItemSystem.ApplyItemStatModifier` returns `Apply`'s `true` ("installed") straight through as claim-success, and `RemoveByModifierId` is now lethal so a +MaxHealth item drop/consume can re-enter `DropAll`→`DropOne` on the in-flight slot and emit a duplicate `ItemDropped` event; a future creator-authored net-negative-MaxHealth ("cursed") item would equip onto/claim a corpse. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; `ApplyItemStatModifier` verified to return the raw `Apply` bool with no post-`IsAlive` check, and the `DropOne`/`UseItem` re-entrancy paths reach the lethal `RemoveByModifierId` before their own event/Destroy writes. Content-gated (Block-If confirmed only `aura_guard.json`=0 and `ring_of_vigor.json`=+50 author MaxHealth). Closure = document the post-condition + audit/guard external `Apply`/`RemoveByModifierId` callers (or a tri-state result).
status: open

### DW-491: The DW-325 ceiling-collapse kill is gated on the ABSOLUTE `EffectiveMaxHealth == 0`, not on a collapse TRANSITION — a live entity legitimately at ceiling 0, or a positive heal applied to one, is lethal
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:566-567 (`if (_world.IsAlive(id) && _world.EffectiveMaxHealth[id] == Fixed.Zero) KillEntity(...)`)
severity: low
reason: The kill fires whenever a MaxHealth-touching modifier leaves the host at ceiling 0 while alive, regardless of sign or prior ceiling — so an entity that legitimately sits at `EffectiveMaxHealth == 0` (e.g. a base-0 / item-sustained host) is killed by ANY MaxHealth modifier, and even a POSITIVE +MaxHealth heal applied to such a host satisfies the gate and is lethal, contradicting the "net-negative-MaxHealth only" wording in the same comment. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; the gate has no sign check on `maxHealthChange` and no "ceiling WAS >0 and dropped to 0 this apply" transition test. Content-gated (no shipped content produces a base-0 live entity; the modifier-delta `!= 0` gate excludes the aura_guard=0 case). Closure = gate on a downward ceiling transition (or on `maxHealthChange < 0`) rather than the absolute value, if a legitimately-ceiling-0 live entity is ever introduced.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle modifier-robustness-and-ceiling) - The kill is now a downward COLLAPSE transition with three conjuncts - net-negative change, prior ceiling > 0 (snapshotted before the accumulate/recompute), new ceiling == 0 - so a legitimately-ceiling-0 host and any positive +MaxHealth grant are no longer lethal. Every real collapse still kills.

### DW-497: EntityPlacer unit create/undo legs `_world.Destroy(box[0])` with no identity re-check — a redo that fails at world capacity leaves a stale boxed id whose next undo destroys whatever unit recycled that slot
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-editor-placement-bounds-height-and-sync.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-editor-placement-bounds-height-and-sync.md`

severity: low
reason: The unit create history closures box the created id and undo via `_world.Destroy(box[0])` with no aliveness/generation re-check. Their redo legs guard `if (r >= 0) box[0] = r`, so if a redo's `DoSpawnCombatUnit`/`RestoreUnit` fails at world capacity, `box[0]` retains a now-stale id and the following undo destroys whatever unit has since recycled that free-list slot — corrupting an unrelated live unit. The sibling ITEM path avoids exactly this by routing undo through the generation-checked `_items.TryResolveRef` before `Destroy`; `EntityWorld.Destroy` has no such guard. Pre-existing across `PlaceUnit`; DW-151 added another instance following the same pattern. Extreme trigger (world at capacity + slot recycle). — Evidence: edge-case + adversarial lenses. Closure = gate the unit undo `Destroy` on the boxed id still being Alive (mirror the item path's resolve-before-destroy), or make `EntityWorld.Destroy` generation-safe.
status: open

### DW-498: No automated regression coverage for the LiveMatchSeed plumbing — the offline reset wiring and the online reseed-to-DEFAULT invariant are guarded only by the manual in-engine gate
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`, 2026-08-03
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/MatchLifecycleController.cs:157 (online `_ctx.World.Rng.Seed(_ctx.LiveMatchSeed)`) + godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:2478-2481 (offline mint/reseed/store wiring)
severity: medium
reason: The pure `MatchSeedProducer` is exhaustively unit-tested, but the two seams that APPLY it have no automated test — no test file references `MatchLifecycleController` and `SimResetTests` only covers the sim-layer `ClearForReset` in isolation. The genuinely-new, load-bearing line is the online reseed at :157: pinning `LiveMatchSeed=DEFAULT` is behavior-identical to the old literal, but reseeding `World.Rng` back to DEFAULT is the new desync-prevention invariant (the session `EntityWorld` is reused, so an offline F5 playtest leaves a per-match seed resident). If a future Godot-layer refactor drops or reorders :157, an online match started after an offline playtest in the same session runs this peer on the leftover per-match seed while other peers run DEFAULT — a silent lockstep desync — with a fully green `dotnet test`. The offline wiring is likewise regressible (reorder before `ClearForReset`, or drop the `Rng.Seed`/`LiveMatchSeed` assignment) with a green suite. The change is CORRECT today (re-verified in-engine 2026-08-03); this is durability of the invariant, not a live defect. — Evidence: verification-gap + adversarial lenses; the online arm is documented as "verified by inspection only" in the spec. Closure = a testable seam (extract the reseed step, or a headless harness for `OnMatchStart`) that pre-dirties `World.Rng` to a non-DEFAULT value and asserts the online entry pins it back to DEFAULT, plus an offline-reset assertion that `LiveMatchSeed == World.Rng.State != DEFAULT`.
status: open

### DW-499: Per-launch varying offline match seed removes cross-launch reproducibility for RNG-touching content, with no debug/env override to PIN the offline seed for repro or A/B verification runs
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`, 2026-08-03

severity: medium
reason: The offline Edit→Play reset now mints a fresh wall-clock-entropy seed every launch (the intended per-match behavior), so two runs of the same authored scenario diverge on any tick-time RNG (combat crits, DSL `random`). This is by design for the bundle's stated intent (a per-match seed), but it weakens the project's in-engine A/B verification methodology — the gate discipline relies on comparing arms of a choice, and RNG-touching content can no longer be reproduced run-to-run because there is no debug/env flag to pin the offline seed to a fixed value. Out of the bundle's intent (which asked for a per-match seed, not a repro pin), hence deferred rather than added. — Evidence: adversarial + verification-gap lenses. Closure = an opt-in override (env var or debug setting) read as the offline entropy when set, so a verification/repro run can fix the seed while normal play stays per-match.
status: open

### DW-504: Modifier period_ticks/period_effect mismatches are only warned about, never rejected, unlike their while_alive Persistent siblings

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs — ValidatePassiveShape (hard rejects) vs CollectModifierWarnings (warnings)
severity: low
reason: A Persistent carrying a period_effect with period_ticks <= 0 is a HARD reject on a while_alive passive, but the same shape is only a warning for a Modifier, and only a warning for a Persistent on an ACTIVE ability. DW-278 made the asymmetry explicit and diagnosed rather than silent, which was its remit, but it is a deliberate scope boundary and not a finished rule: an author who ignores the warning still ships an inert period. Promoting any of these to errors is a potentially content-breaking gate change that wants its own decision — and it is currently FREE, because all shipped content is clean today (no shipped Modifier has a period_effect), so the cost only rises as content lands.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Promote the period mismatch to a hard reject now while content is clean — Move the CollectModifierWarnings period_ticks<=0 (and period_ticks>0 with no period_effect) cases into ValidatePassiveShape-style hard rejects for Modifiers and active-ability Persistents, matching the while_alive rule.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-504 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified live first: CollectModifierWarnings emitted the mismatch as a non-fatal warning while ValidatePassiveShape hard-rejected the identical shape on a while_alive Persistent, so the rule depended on where the shape appeared. Implemented the recorded owner decision exactly and no wider — three cases are now hard rejects for EVERY ability: (a) a Modifier with a period_effect and period_ticks <= 0, (b) a Modifier with period_ticks > 0 and no period_effect, (c) a Persistent with a period_effect and period_ticks <= 0 (previously a reject only on while_alive). Mechanism: the renamed CollectModifierDiagnostics/CollectPersistentDiagnostics route those cases into a fatal list on the existing single walk; Validate reports it AFTER ValidatePassiveShape (so the while_alive message keeps precedence and the defect is never double-reported) and after WalkGraph's inline structural errors. Every other DW-278 warning with a live non-inert reading deliberately stays non-fatal. Coverage: new AbilityPeriodMismatchRejectTests.cs (14 tests), proven RED against the pre-fix validator (9/14 failed); the three AbilityInertContentWarningTests cases encoding the old warn-only behaviour were removed as future false-greens and MultipleFootgunsInOneGraph_AllSurface re-armed with shapes that are still warnings. Determinism: content-gate logic only, no data shape changed, nothing folded touched; no shipped ability carries the shape (aura_guard.json is the well-formed no-period shape; furnace_pour/furnace_trickle pair period_ticks 15 with a period_effect) so no content moves and no golden moved. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5180/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline +14 -3.

### DW-505: ValidateComplete's mesh_path error mis-routes the wizard: the `faction '<id>'.` prefix defeats StepForError, and the existing test asserts a message shape the validator never produces

severity: medium
reason: ValidateComplete emits "faction 'x'.mesh_path: unit 'grunt' is missing mesh_path…", but StepForError only routes to the Roster step when the message STARTS WITH "unit '" — so in production a missing UNIT mesh_path sends the author to the Buildings & Tech step. Note the new MeshAssetLint messages deliberately use the un-prefixed "unit '…'"/"building '…'" shape and a test asserts they route correctly, so the two axes now disagree.

### DW-511: ServerChecksumCollector has no ACCEPT_WINDOW guard, so a client can evict honest in-flight comparison windows with far-future checksum ticks

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/ServerChecksumCollector.cs:115-133 (Record) — compare the sibling guard at godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/MergedTickBuilder.cs:128-130
severity: high
reason: Record accepts any checksum tick a client claims and evicts the ring bucket it lands on, so a single misbehaving or malicious client can silently destroy the honest majority's in-flight comparison windows and blind the desync guard (a grief/starvation vector, sibling of DW-435/DW-436 on the command path). Pre-existing and unrelated to either entry the discovering bundle closed, and NOT fixable by copying MergedTickBuilder's ACCEPT_WINDOW: the collector's _resolvedThrough starts at -1 while real checksum ticks start at the checksum interval, so a naive window rejects the first legitimate report of every match. A correct fix must gate acceptance on a real frontier (e.g. MergedTickBuilder.EmittedThrough) and needs its own design + tests. DW-239's fix makes the symptom OBSERVABLE (each eviction now logs an ABANDONED line and increments AbandonedWindows) but does not reject the input.
status: open

### DW-512: MovementSystem's separation query has the same over-cap arbitrariness DW-249 described — and unlike SearchArea its output DOES feed SimChecksum

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03

severity: medium
reason: The unfiltered SpatialHash.QueryRadius keeps the first 32 neighbours in cell-scan order, so in a crowd denser than 32 units inside a 2.0 radius (the 500-2000-entity target is well past that) WHICH neighbours push a unit is decided by grid geometry rather than any defined rule. It is deterministic across peers (same grid, same positions) so it is NOT a desync — it is a steering-quality/fairness issue. Deliberately left byte-identical by the searcharea-target-selection-correctness bundle because separation output flows into Position, a SimChecksum input, so re-ruling the truncation or raising the buffer moves every movement golden (formation-separation, ai-active, the merged-N goldens) — that needs its own deliberate re-baseline story, which the burn-down brief forbids. The pure API to consume already exists: SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter>, and both QueryRadius overloads now carry a doc note pointing callers at it.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-04 Keep byte-identical (deterministic, not a desync — only a fairness nicety)

### DW-521: `git stash` is SHARED across every burn-down worktree, so parallel bundle agents silently steal and drop each other's uncommitted work

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: .claude/workflows/dw-burndown.workflow.js + the per-agent bundle brief (agent instructions); .git/refs/stash (one stack for all ~80 worktrees)
severity: high
reason: `refs/stash` lives in the shared common .git directory, NOT per-worktree, so a `git stash push` from any one of the parallel bundle worktrees lands on ONE global stack and a `git stash pop` in a different worktree applies whatever another agent pushed last and DROPS that agent's entry. This fired live in a single chunk, in both directions: worktree wf_5d8656b5-2c0-21 popped wf_5d8656b5-2c0-19's validator WIP (ItemDefinitionValidator.cs / UnitDefinitionValidator.cs / DefinitionValidatorStrictBoundsTests.cs) into its own tree while -19 concurrently popped -21's, and both had to be hand-repaired. Both agents recovered with zero work lost, but the unnoticed failure modes are severe: an agent that commits after a bad pop silently ships ANOTHER bundle's code inside its own merge (with a green gate, because the foreign code compiles), and an agent whose entry was dropped loses its work to gc. The proximate cause is the baseline drift in DW-502 — agents stash precisely to measure the pristine Tier-1 baseline the brief states wrongly. Fix = an explicit prohibition in the agent brief (never `git stash` in a burn-down worktree; copy files to the scratchpad, or commit-then-reset, or measure the baseline in a throwaway clone) plus stating a correct per-base baseline so nobody needs to measure it. Recovery recipe worth putting in the brief too: `git stash list --format="%H %gd %gs"` to snapshot SHAs, `git stash store -m "<original message>" <sha>` to put a wrongly-dropped entry back, and `git diff <stash>^1 <stash>` plus `git show <stash>^3:<path>` to extract your own work without trusting the stash index again.
status: open

### DW-532: DW-148's movement confinement can strand a worker holding a gather-slot reservation forever, re-opening the folded-capacity leak DW-207 closed in the same merge

origin: workflow burn-down post-merge review, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs:163-174 (`IsBlockedOutside` confinement) × godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:124-143 (`TickMovingToResource`)
severity: medium
reason: Emergent cross-bundle interaction, confirmed by reading both merged sides; neither bundle's agent could see it (DW-148 owned the confinement in scenario-validator-spawn-and-bounds, DW-80/DW-207 owned the release paths in gathering-worker-lifecycle, and the latter branched from 024025e before the former merged). `ScenarioApplier` deliberately only `_log.Warn()`s a spawn inside a blocked cell and applies the placement anyway (ScenarioApplier.cs:174-176: "silently refusing to spawn authored content would be strictly worse"), while `MovementSystem` now CONFINES such a unit via `IsBlockedOutside(fromCell, ...)`. Confinement still permits walking out into a CLEAR neighbour, so the trap needs a blocked region at least 3 cells across with the worker on an INTERIOR cell — then the step and both wall-slide axes all resolve to foreign blocked cells and line 173 hard-stops it in place every tick. `GatheringSystem.TickIdle` → `AssignToNode` (GatheringSystem.cs:366-374) has already incremented `_nodes.AssignedGatherers[node]` — a SimChecksum-folded value — and set `MovingToResource`. `TickMovingToResource` releases only on `node < 0 || !_nodes.Active[node]` (:129-134), so a worker that can never close to `ARRIVE_AT_NODE_SQR` holds the reservation for the whole match. None of the four release paths the bundle enumerates as exhaustive at GatheringSystem.cs:22-27 can fire: the tick loop never leaves `MovingToResource`, `EntityWorld.OnDestroy` needs a death, `BuildingSystem.QueueWorkerBuild` needs a Build order, and DW-80's `STREAMING_GATE_GRACE_TICKS` re-idle sits inside `TickGathering` (:182-190), reachable only AFTER arrival. `FindBestNode` skips a node at `AssignedGatherers >= MaxGatherers` (:434, shipped default 4), so enough stranded workers starve that node for EVERY faction — the precise starvation DW-207 was written to eliminate. Pre-DW-148 the same worker was exempt from blocking and simply walked out. Needs a real authored map to trigger (the validator only warns), which is why it is medium not high. Likely fix: bound the `MovingToResource` leg the way DW-80 bounded the gate park — a no-progress tick counter that releases the slot and re-idles — rather than weakening the confinement.
status: open

### DW-533: Scenario enums went fail-closed (`allowIntegerValues:false`) while both production `LoadFromFile` callers still branch on `== null` for "parse-failed", so a numeric enum aborts boot instead of taking the fallback

origin: workflow burn-down post-merge review, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentJson.cs:119 (`BuildScenario`) vs godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:88-94 and godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:2796-2798
severity: low
reason: DW-274 replaced `ScenarioSerializer`'s deleted private `_options` — whose converter was the parameterless `new JsonStringEnumConverter()`, i.e. `allowIntegerValues: true` — with `new JsonStringEnumConverter(namingPolicy: null, allowIntegerValues: false)`. The tightening itself is correct and deliberate (name-only authoring, fail-closed) and the bundle correctly fixed `LoadFromFile`'s doc to admit that malformed input propagates. What was not updated is the two production callers, which still code to the OLD contract. `ScenarioSerializer.LoadFromFile` (:44-49) has no try/catch, so a scenario carrying `"win_condition": 0` (or a numeric `type`/`scope` on a scenario variable — ScenarioData.cs:534/538/596/714) now throws `JsonException` past `ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:88` and past `ScenePhaseRunner.Run` (no try/catch), so the client aborts `_Ready` mid-phase with a half-initialised scene instead of printing "Scenario not found or failed to parse … using defaults" and booting the fallback mirror; the dedicated server aborts instead of degrading to relay+quorum. `SkirmishCatalog.cs:106` is the only caller already wrapped. Low because every shipped map and the editor's own writer emit enum NAMES (verified: no numeric enum values under godot/resources/data/scenarios/), so this only fires on hand-edited or externally generated `user://` content — but that is exactly the content the located-fallback path exists to survive. Fix is to catch `JsonException` at the `LoadFromFile` boundary (or in both callers) and map it to the existing null/fallback contract, keeping the located error message.

### DW-534: `QueryRadiusLowestIds` drops the `count < maxResults` scan bound with no authored radius cap anywhere, so a wide-radius SearchArea scans every entity in radius on a 30 Hz lockstep path

origin: workflow burn-down post-merge review, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Navigation/SpatialHash.cs:276-306 (bound deliberately absent; contrast `QueryRadius` at :208)
severity: low
reason: The missing bound is REQUIRED by the global-lowest-ids contract DW-249/250/252 established — a full buffer must not end the scan, because a later candidate may still be lower-id — and is correctly documented as such at :276-278. The gap is that it was also the only cost ceiling, and nothing else bounds the work: `cellRadius = (radius / CELL_SIZE).ToInt() + 1` is limited only by the `GRID_DIM` bounds checks (:265/:270), and no radius bound exists in `AbilityValidator` or `EffectBounds` (grepped both) — the authoring spin row is `AddSpinRow(card, "Radius", 0, FixedSpinMax, ...)` (AbilityEditorPanel.Advanced.cs:279) and `FixedJsonConverter` admits anything in the 16.16 range. With `GRID_DIM = 32` and `CELL_SIZE_F = 10`, an authored radius >= 320 visits all 1024 cells with no early exit, evaluating `filter.Accepts` (`DomainClassifier.Of` + `TagGate.Intersects` + `AllianceStore.AreAllied`, TargetMatcher.cs:37-78) for every alive entity up to `MAX_ENTITIES = 4096`, plus up to 64 insertion shifts per accepted match once the buffer fills. Nested one level (`MaxSearchAreaDepth = 2`) that is 64 outer targets × N candidates per cast versus roughly 64 candidates plus a cell walk before. Fully deterministic, so NOT a desync risk — but it is a 30 Hz lockstep hot path where a tick overrun stalls every peer through the adaptive-delay/stall machinery rather than degrading locally. Cheapest fix is an authored-radius cap validated at load (an `EffectCaps.MaxSearchRadius` folded into `RulesetHash`, since it is a structural bound), which bounds `cellRadius` without touching the selection contract.
status: open

### DW-543: Per-occurrence trigger dispatch keeps running after fuel exhaustion within one trigger, stretching the whole-trigger-boundary contract across N occurrences
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/ScenarioDirector.cs — EvaluateTriggers, the param-reading occurrence loop
severity: low
reason: FuelExhausted is checked only at the sweep's per-trigger boundary, so a param-reading trigger that exhausts the budget mid-occurrence keeps dispatching its remaining matching occurrences that tick (each a full FireTrigger). Deterministic and arguably 'the in-flight trigger completes', but it stretches the documented whole-trigger-boundary contract across N occurrences of a single trigger, making the per-tick fuel ceiling less honest than it reads. Out of the dsl-runtime-fuel-hardening bundle's scope (named by none of its five entries); left unchanged to avoid altering established dispatch semantics without a recorded owner decision. Closure = an owner decision on whether the boundary is per-trigger or per-occurrence, then make the check match it.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Halt at occurrence granularity — Move the FuelExhausted check inside the occurrence loop so an exhausted budget stops dispatching further occurrences of the same trigger, tightening the per-tick ceiling to match the documented contract.
resolution: closed by bundle scenariodirector-fuel-requeue (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified LIVE first, then implemented to the recorded ledger decision (DW-543 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger `decision:` line was the authority and was followed literally). Confirmed: ScenarioDirector.EvaluateTriggers checked `_loopState.FuelExhausted` only at the sweep's per-TRIGGER boundary (top of the exec loop), so a param-reading trigger's per-occurrence loop kept dispatching every remaining matching occurrence after the budget was spent, each a full FireTrigger. Fix: the check now runs INSIDE the occurrence loop, after the run-once/cooldown gate (so a gate-blocked skip stays authored semantics) and before the batched-suppression check. On exhaustion it calls the existing DW-349 arm `RequeueEdgeEventsFor(idx, ex, fromEvent: e)`, so the unconsumed EDGE occurrences persist targeted at that trigger; the sweep's own top-of-loop check then persists the skipped tail from idx+1 — tightening the ceiling therefore loses nothing. Determinism: no golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash value moved; every golden/hash/checksum test passed unchanged, including the DW-349 goldens-safety proof PolledThresholds_AreNeverPersisted_AndFuelSkipBehaviorIsUnchanged. Coverage: new Godot-free godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Dsl/DslFuelOccurrenceHaltTests.cs (3 tests) whose fixtures pre-burn 63 x 257 = 16191 of the 16384-op budget with whole-trigger burns keyed on a switchable P2 threshold, so the halt lands on a hand-computable dispatch; teeth proven by temporarily neutering the production code (file copy to scratchpad, then restored) — all 3 FAIL with both fixes neutered. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5172 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (338.73 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 3 new. Follow-ons filed as DW-685 (the occurrence loop never re-checks the trigger-enabled mask) and DW-686 (RequeueEdgeEventsFor now has three callers all relying on an undocumented pre-checked-gate precondition).

### DW-545: DrainWorkList still abandons remaining same-tick custom occurrences on fuel exhaustion — a surviving loss class DW-349 did not close
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/ScenarioDirector.cs — DrainWorkList
severity: medium
reason: Fuel exhaustion during the custom-event drain abandons the remaining same-tick work items (documented as an accepted-loss class in the method doc). status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Extend re-queue rail to custom occurrences — Persist fuel-dropped same-tick custom occurrences through the DW-349 re-queue rail and re-validate the cascade-bound analysis so custom events get the same edge-parity as base events.
resolution: closed by bundle scenariodirector-fuel-requeue (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified LIVE first, then implemented to the recorded ledger decision (DW-545 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger `decision:` line was the authority and was followed literally). Confirmed: DrainWorkList's per-dispatch fuel check did a bare `return`, abandoning the rest of the same-tick work list (the method doc named it an accepted loss). Fix: the halt now persists everything. The occurrence caught mid-dispatch rides a NEW reserved rail, `EventBounds.CustomRequeueRailBase (0x100000) + resumeExec * MaxCustomEvents + eventIndex`, which packs the registry index and the RESUME exec into the queue's code lane so raiser and the full P0..P3 payload keep their own lanes — a max-param custom event persists losslessly, where the DW-349 rail's P3-as-target trick has no free slot on a custom occurrence. Items the halt never STARTED persist under their plain registry index, i.e. as ordinary next-tick occurrences, so the common case adds no new code shape to the folded queue. The tick-start dequeue decodes the rail into a work item carrying TargetExec as a resume floor; DrainWorkList starts its subscriber scan there, so subscribers already served on the drop tick can never double-fire. Cascade bound re-validated (the decision's second half) and written into the method doc: persistence DEFERS, never amplifies — at most one queue row per abandoned occurrence, redelivered as a root occurrence whose transitive same-tick cost the load-time MaxCascadeOps proof already bounds, with MaxNextTickEventQueue drop-newest capping how many roots can persist. Determinism: no golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash value moved; the new rail rows can only exist on a tick that exhausts the 16384-op DSL budget, which no shipped content or golden fixture does, and the DW-349 proof PolledThresholds_AreNeverPersisted_AndFuelSkipBehaviorIsUnchanged still passes. Coverage: new Godot-free godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Dsl/DslFuelOccurrenceHaltTests.cs (3 tests); teeth proven by temporarily neutering the production code (file copy to scratchpad, then restored) — all 3 FAIL with both fixes neutered, and with ONLY the resume-exec neutered (persist untargeted) the two custom-drain tests FAIL with 448 and 512 instead of 384, proving the resume encoding is what prevents double-firing already-served subscribers. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5172 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 3 new. Follow-on filed as DW-684 (custom-occurrence re-queue parity is capped by the 64-row queue while the work list holds 1024).

### DW-560: ContentPackager.Pack destroys a pre-existing output zip before writing the new one (non-atomic export output)
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03

reason: Same non-atomic-write family as DW-421 but on Pack's OUTPUT rather than RewriteManifest's in-place edit: an existing export at outputZipPath is deleted up front, so a throw mid-write leaves the creator's previous export destroyed and a partial zip on disk. Reachable in practice because the non-hashed sources (screenshot, faction files, thumbnail) are still re-read at write time, so one of them being deleted or locked between enumeration and the write loop throws after the old export is already gone. Out of the contentpackager-atomic-and-symmetry bundle's scope, which covered RewriteManifest atomicity, the hash TOCTOU, and pack/unpack gate symmetry - not Pack output staging. Closure = the same stage-to-temp-then-atomic-File.Move pattern RewriteManifest now uses, so a failed export leaves the prior export byte-identical.
status: open

### DW-561: ItemCardPanel.LoadItemsFromDir bypasses the fail-closed ItemLoader/Validate gate, admitting hostile or invalid hand-authored defs into the editable set
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/ItemCardPanel.cs:184-185
reason: The panel deserializes item JSON raw with no Validate gate, so an invalid or hostile hand-authored def enters the editable set silently - asymmetric with ItemRegistry.LoadFromDirectory, which validates and reports drops via onSkipped (DW-455). Bind->Revalidate does badge the offending fields and Save stays disabled, and the one concrete filesystem sink this fed (the _originalId rename-cleanup File.Delete, reachable with an id like '../../evil') was closed under DW-456, so this is not currently fail-open. It is also plausibly deliberate: an ungated load is what lets a creator open and repair a broken file, which a fail-closed loader would make impossible. Closure = a ledger decision on the intended posture - either keep the raw load and document it as the repair path, or route through ItemLoader with a visible skipped-files warning like the registry - rather than a silent asymmetry between the two loaders.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-04 Gate the load fail-closed — Route LoadItemsFromDir through the ItemLoader/Validate gate with onSkipped reporting so invalid/hostile defs are dropped and reported at load, matching ItemRegistry.LoadFromDirectory.

### DW-566: FlowFieldBridge’s arrival check uses the shared field’s pinned GoalWorld, not the unit’s own exact goal

Safe today by construction: the only cross-tick holder of a packed ENTITY ref is `WinConditionSystem._leaderRef`, which the SP load path re-packs at generation 0 during its fresh apply-time re-configure (`ClearForReset` zeroes generations; apply-time spawns append at gen 0), and a resolved leader's death latches its FOLDED `WinStateStore` verdict on the same tick it dies - so no save boundary can separate a bumped generation from its persisted consequence. The trap is future work: the moment any story stores a packed ENTITY ref in persisted or folded state (the way packed BUILDING refs already live in the persisted `CommandTarget` lane), `EntityWorld.Generation` MUST join the `SaveGameState` entity lanes or a reload will resolve stale refs as live. Documented on the field; adding the lane now would churn the save format for zero present benefit. Closure = add the lane at that point, or add a gate test asserting no packed entity ref reaches persisted or folded state.
status: open

### DW-590: Allied-KotH concede by the team REP orphans the rep-keyed hold accumulator

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/WinConditionSystem.cs - UpdateKothCounters/TeamRep + KothWinningTeam
severity: medium
reason: Pre-existing Story 11.2 x 7.12 interaction, NOT introduced or worsened by the DW-188 bundle: if the lowest-slot (rep) faction of an allied team latches LOST via CONCEDE while a live ally keeps sole-holding the zone, `UpdateKothCounters` keeps accruing hold ticks on the LOST rep (`TeamRep` ignores verdicts) but `KothWinningTeam` only reads verdict-NONE factions, so the ally's hold can never reach the win and the match hangs. Fixing it means touching the hold-race WIN path (e.g. re-repping to the lowest verdict-NONE member, which moves folded `KothHoldTicks` values) - exactly what the DW-188 decision said not to perturb - and concede-with-teams semantics deserve their own decision. The DW-188 wipeout fallback deliberately avoids this class via its team-scoped guard. Closure = a design decision on allied-KotH concede semantics, then a hold-race-path change with an explicit golden/checksum review.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-05 Re-rep KothHoldTicks to the lowest verdict-NONE team member — Make TeamRep/KothWinningTeam agree by re-keying the accumulator to the lowest verdict-NONE ally when the rep latches LOST (moving folded KothHoldTicks), then re-record affected goldens.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-590 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05), commit 4ce6b8d4. Defect confirmed live: UpdateKothCounters keyed the contiguous sole-hold count on TeamRep = the lowest-slot member full stop, while KothWinningTeam reads only verdict-NONE factions, so when the rep latched LOST out-of-band (Story 11.2 CONCEDE via OrderApplier, or the DSL `defeat` leaf) the count kept accruing on the dead rep while the live sole-holding ally was zeroed every tick as a non-rep — and with 2 live teams ApplyLastTeamStanding no-ops, so the match hung forever. Fix (godot/src/Core/WinConditionSystem.cs, 2 methods + 1 helper): TeamRep now returns the lowest-slot UNRESOLVED member, falling back to the historic lowest-slot member when every member is resolved; new TeamHoldTicks reads the team's live count as the max over active members (at most one slot per team is ever non-zero) so a re-rep CARRIES the count rather than restarting at zero, while a contest that already zeroed the counter correctly restarts the ally at 1. Determinism: NO golden was re-recorded and none moved — the decision's "then re-record affected goldens" clause proved unnecessary, because folded KothHoldTicks values are byte-identical wherever the old rep was already correct (every all-unresolved team, and every FFA teams-of-1 slot, which is why the fallback keeps the historic slot); independently confirmed no golden scenario or shipped resource uses the KingOfTheHill preset and no golden mutates AllianceStore.TeamId. SimChecksum AlgoVersion, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash untouched. Scope held: the DW-188 team-scoped wipeout guard was NOT narrowed even though its orphan rationale is now moot (that is a different loss rule than DW-188 recorded); only its comment was updated to say why it stays. Tests: new Godot-free KothRepReKeyTests.cs (6 tests; concedes drive the REAL OrderApplier wire path, not a hand-poked verdict), red-verified 4 failed / 2 passed against the pre-fix file — the 4 red ones being the headline re-rep-and-win case, the two-successive-concedes lowest-unresolved ordering pin, the contest-before-concede live-carry pin, and the two-run determinism fold (which hangs pre-fix); the 2 that pass on both sides are the intentional fold-neutrality pins. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5175/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passes in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 6 new.

A faithful fix needs a recordable choke point for offline apply-now orders (some sites bypass OrderApplier entirely), per-tick per-faction coalescing under the frozen 32-order sub-bundle budget (offline order volume is unbounded, so naive per-order sub-bundles would trip the new DW-432 overflow throw past 8 orders/tick), exact faction stamping (replay apply authorizes against the sub-bundle faction), and in-engine verification - i.e. a bmad-loop story touching src/UI/**, not a Godot-free bundle. status: open

### DW-605: Online lockstep silently drops orders past 32 per tick, so large box-select commands truncate with no player feedback
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/LockstepManager.cs:318-319 (EnqueueOrder: `if (_pendingCount < TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS)` with no else branch and no denial cue)
severity: medium
reason: Found during the DW-429 analysis. Online, a command issued against more than 32 units in one tick (box-select 40 units + right-click = 40 per-unit orders) silently drops orders 33+: those units never move and the player gets no OrderDenied cue, while the offline apply-now path applies all 40. It is deterministic (the drop happens client-side before send) so it is not a desync, but it is a live/offline behavior divergence and a silent-drop UX gap on a very ordinary RTS input. Pre-existing and orthogonal to the replay bundle's scope, so not touched. Closure = either coalesce/queue the overflow into the next tick or surface an explicit denial cue, and pin the chosen behavior with a test.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-05 Coalesce/queue overflow across ticks — Coalesce or queue orders beyond 32 into subsequent ticks so all selected units eventually receive the command, matching offline apply-now completeness.
scoping-note (owner, 2026-08-05): FIRST establish whether `TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS = 32` caps *orders* or *units* — it changes the implementation completely and the wrong reading builds the wrong thing. If one right-click over N selected units currently emits N separate order entries, the correct fix is NOT a cross-tick queue: it is emitting ONE order carrying a unit-ID list, which is how lockstep RTS engines normally do this, is smaller, and removes the cap pressure entirely rather than spreading it. Only if the 32 are genuinely distinct commands does cross-tick coalescing apply. Rejected option 1 (OrderDenied cue) deliberately: box-select-and-right-click is the core RTS interaction and 40 units is a small army against a 500-2000 entity target, so a denial cue would fire constantly in normal play — it labels the defect rather than fixing it, and is not a stable resting place at target scale.

### DW-609: DW-458's prune-and-reconcile does not reach trigger_graph IR or custom_events.allowed_raisers, so those can still carry refs to dropped slots
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/Skirmish/SkirmishSetupToScenario.cs (reconcile helpers)
severity: low
reason: The DW-458 prune-and-reconcile covers the flat `Triggers` array, the win-condition spec, and Income node owners. A base map authoring graph-IR triggers (`ScenarioData.TriggerGraphJson`) or `custom_events.allowed_raisers` can still carry faction refs to dropped slots after a reduced-player launch: the boot validator only engine-ceiling-gates those (no declared-slot check), so nothing rejects and the dangling refs are inert (they never match or raise) — but they are semantically stale and a later validator tightening would surface them as boot rejections. Deliberately out of the bundle's scope because reconciling graph IR means parsing and rewriting TriggerGraph node params; no shipped map authors either block today. Closure = extend the reconcile pass over TriggerGraphJson node params and allowed_raisers, or add a declared-slot check to the boot validator so a stale graph fails loudly.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by the total-relabel fix in SkirmishSetupToScenario (ReconcileCustomEvents + ReconcileTriggerGraphJson). The renumber itself is load-bearing (FactionRegistry active span, LocalFactionPolicy's Player1-human hardwire, TeamColorPalette indexing) so it stays; what changes is that the relabel is now TOTAL across every per-slot channel, which yields exactly the WC3/modern-RTS guarantee -- a reference designates the player the author meant, or an empty seat, never a DIFFERENT player. Graph structure is untouched (no node/edge pruning): survivors remap through slotMap, dropped refs canonicalize to the vacant seat k. Note the precise scope: dropped ordinals were ALREADY inert (d >= k always, since pairing takes the k lowest), so the real corruption fixed here is the renumbered SURVIVOR. Class guard: SkirmishGraphReconcileTests.EveryNodeTypeWithAFactionField_IsCoveredByTheReconcile reflects over NodeBase subclasses and fails if a new Faction-carrying node kind is added without being handled -- the silence that let DW-458 ship incomplete cannot recur. 14 tests, 6 proven RED against the un-reconciled build; Tier-1 4858/0/1, no golden moved.
seen-again: 2026-08-04 (post-merge review sweep of merge 0a06b2d) — two lenses re-reported this gap, and verification sharpens it beyond the "inert" framing above: the validator accepts NON-contiguous unique slot ordinals (ScenarioValidator.cs:262-283) and the editor produces them as a first-class state (ScenarioData.RemoveStartSlot removes by Slot value with no renumber — its doc names "a non-contiguous {0,1,3} set"). On such a map Build's positional pairing renumbers the surviving slots (authored {0,2,5} → {0→0, 2→1, 5→2}); the flat Triggers channel is rewritten but TriggerGraphJson faction fields and CustomEvents[].AllowedRaisers are not, so a stale ref lands on a LIVE renumbered player instead of an empty seat: a graph trigger keyed to a surviving original ordinal fires for the wrong player, and event-raise authorization silently transfers — the author-intended raiser is dropped at TryEnqueueExternalDslEvent's Array.IndexOf auth check (ScenarioDirector.cs:487-491) with no error or log, while the player renumbered onto the stale ordinal inherits it. Only on contiguous-from-0 maps does the pairing stay prefix-identity and the inert framing hold. Treat as severity medium for triage (wrong-player dispatch/authorization is semantic corruption of creator content, not mere staleness); closure unchanged. No separate entry filed.

### DW-616: DeathFeed has the identical silent-drop-when-full ring with no priority lane, and its drops are checksum-visible
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/DeathFeed.cs:35
severity: medium
reason: `MAX_DEATHS = 256` with the same drop-when-full shape as the pre-DW-469 CombatEventQueue, and its own doc comment says the cap mirrors that queue. Unlike the event queue this one has a FOLDED consequence — a dropped DeathRecord awards no hero XP, and XP is in SimChecksum — so a >256-death tick is a (self-healing, low-likelihood) determinism-visible feedback loss. Out of the combat-event-queue-capacity bundle's scope and NOT changed there: any fix moves folded XP and needs its own deliberate golden analysis. Closure = a capacity/priority design for DeathFeed with the golden work costed in.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-05 Design capacity/priority fix with golden work costed — Raise/priority-lane DeathFeed capacity (or make overflow deterministic-and-lossless) and run the deliberate SimChecksum/golden re-baseline analysis for the folded XP change.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-616 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified still open: DeathFeed.cs:35 still carried `MAX_DEATHS = 256` with a bare drop-when-full Push and a doc comment still claiming the cap "mirrors CombatEventQueue" — a claim DW-469 had already invalidated on the queue side. Defect confirmed REAL, not cosmetic: DeathFeed itself is unfolded (HeroXpSystem drains + Clears it in-tick) but the XP a DeathRecord pays IS folded — HeroStore.Xp/Level and the permanent growth-modifier stacks flow into SimChecksum (SimChecksum.cs:335 folds world.XpBounty explicitly) — so a >256-death tick silently withheld folded feedback. Fix: chose LOSSLESS, not a priority lane — a DW-469-style reserve is inapplicable because every death carries the identical kind of folded consequence, so there is no low-value class to sacrifice. Push now grows the backing array by amortized doubling from INITIAL_CAPACITY = 256 and never drops; growth is a pure function of the push sequence, preserves order index-for-index (Array.Copy, matching the ProjectileStore/BuildingStore house pattern), and capacity is exposed only as a diagnostic `Capacity` property — never folded, serialized or replicated, so two peers that grew differently still credit identical XP. Retained capacity is bounded by peak deaths in one tick (bounded by KillEntity calls, <= EntityWorld.MAX_ENTITIES = 4096 plus in-tick churn). GOLDEN RE-BASELINE ANALYSIS (the half the decision costed in): ZERO goldens move, no re-record needed. Everything the sim can observe about the feed is Count and Get over [0,Count); for the first 256 pushes both come from the exact same append the fixed ring did with no reallocation in between, so any tick at or under the old cap yields a bit-identical HeroXpSystem credit pass and therefore a bit-identical SimChecksum — the change is observable ONLY on a tick that would previously have overflowed, which no recorded golden or replay scenario contains. Pinned permanently by Push_AtInitialCapacity_DoesNotGrow_SoSubCapTicksAreBitIdenticalToThePreFixRing (asserts Count==256 AND Capacity==256) and confirmed empirically: all 31 .golden.txt-backed test classes plus GoldenChecksumReplay, ReBaselineDifferentialGuard, StartStateHash and CanonicalModelHash passed untouched. Tests: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Combat/DeathFeedCapacityTests.cs, 6 Godot-free cases, proven to bite by temporarily restoring the drop-when-full Push — 4 of 6 FAIL pre-fix (no-silent-drop, order-preserved-across-the-growth-boundary, overflow-deaths-credit-folded-hero-XP, different-capacities-drain-identically); the other 2 are the deliberate no-golden-move / Clear-posture pins that must pass in both worlds. Also corrected DeathLog.cs's now-stale doc line claiming its CAPACITY is "the DeathFeed cap" (comment only — DeathLog behaviour is DW-367's and deliberately untouched, since changing it would move trigger-visible unit_dies events; filed as DW-674). Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5175/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 6 new, no pre-existing test changed state.
