### DW-620: Invulnerable does not cover the ModifierStore ceiling-collapse kill or direct_hp_delta/cost_health self-costs
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:~575 (EffectiveMaxHealth==0 → DamageResolver.KillEntity); godot/src/Effects/DirectHpDeltaEffect.cs:34; godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs (cost_health debit)
severity: medium
reason: Recorded as an explicit DW-266 scope boundary rather than an oversight: the recorded decision routes Invulnerable to DamageResolver, so it now blocks all DAMAGE, but a -MaxHealth debuff that collapses the ceiling to 0 still kills an invulnerable unit (DW-325's zombie-kill path calls KillEntity directly, bypassing Apply), and self-costs still spend HP. Both are arguably correct (a self-cost is not damage), but the ceiling-collapse case is a genuine open question. Closure = a later balance/status story settles whether Invulnerable is damage-immunity or death-immunity, and pins it with a test either way.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-620 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Implemented the recorded owner decision verbatim: Invulnerable is DEATH-immunity, so the guard moved to the single death primitive rather than being duplicated at each direct-kill site. Verified against current code first — DW-266's gate really does sit only on DamageResolver.Apply (DamageResolver.cs:89), and two callers reach the death sequence without passing through it: ModifierStore.ApplyStatDeltas's DW-325 ceiling-collapse kill (ModifierStore.cs:760) and AbilityCastSystem's deferred self-lethal cost_health death (AbilityCastSystem.cs:442); both killed an invulnerable unit outright. The entry's third named location, DirectHpDeltaEffect.cs:34, was already correct (it clamps to [0, MaxHealth] and never fires a death sequence), so the decision's "leave self-costs spend-able" half needed no change there. Fix: DamageResolver.KillEntity now refuses the kill when StatusFlagsOf carries Invulnerable, placed ahead of every write in the sequence so a refused kill is a strict no-op — no killer attribution, no DeathLog record, no UnitKilled/HeroFell event, no RecordKill, no DeathFeed push, no Destroy. One home covers both current direct callers and any future one; unreachable from Apply (its own DW-266 guard returns first). One consequence had to be handled or the change would have introduced a new defect: AbilityCastSystem returned unconditionally after the self-lethal KillEntity, so a death-immune caster would have been left on NEGATIVE health with no cooldown started — free to re-cast every tick and walk Health toward the Fixed underflow. The tail now re-checks IsAlive and floors the pool at 0 (the DirectHpDeltaEffect self-cost convention), then falls through to the normal cooldown/feedback tail; byte-identical for a killable caster. Determinism: nothing re-recorded, no golden touched — the new branch is entered only when StatusFlagsOf carries Invulnerable, which no recorded golden sets (the pre-existing DW-266 damage-path guard already relies on and demonstrates that), and no SoA field or fold changed, so SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash are untouched. Coverage: new Godot-free InvulnerableDeathImmunityTests (4 cases), each proven RED by temporarily disabling the guard (4/4 failed, then restored) — the primitive's refused-kill-is-a-no-op plus kills-once-the-flag-drops; the ceiling collapse where the immune host survives at ceiling 0 while a non-immune twin in the same world dies (teeth against simply disabling DW-325); the collapse turning lethal again once an AUTHORED invulnerability modifier expires through the real store path; and the self-lethal cast spending its health, damaging its target, surviving at exactly 0, and starting its cooldown. Gate: build succeeded (6 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors); suite 5174 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5170/0/1 baseline — exactly the 4 new tests, no flake. Follow-ons filed as DW-675 (stale Invulnerable HUD tooltip), DW-676 (a death-immune host left permanently at 0 HP with no re-kill on flag expiry) and DW-677 (buildings have no status-flag channel to gate on).
decision: 2026-08-05 Invulnerable = death-immunity: also block the ceiling-collapse KillEntity path — Guard the ModifierStore EffectiveMaxHealth==0 -> KillEntity path (and any direct KillEntity) against StatusFlags.Invulnerable, leaving self-costs as spend-able, and pin with a test.

### DW-622: DropDirective applyAtTick is NOT the first idle tick when the dropped peer led the frontier — the doc contract and the UI marker both over-claim

That justification only holds when the dropped peer was AT or BEHIND the merge frontier. When it was racing ahead (the DW-412 case), its real commands are already buffered for ticks well past the marker: the new DirectiveMarker_IsTheEmittedHighWater_NotTheRacersLead pins applyAtTick==3 while the peer's real orders still execute through tick 30. Not a desync — the client never hard-zeros at the marker, it only raises OnPlayerDropped for UI and echoes the value in its ACK, and the merged stream stays authoritative — so this is an observability/doc-accuracy gap ("Player2 frozen at tick 3" while Player2 acts until tick 30). status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-623 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified live first: the defect was real and unfixed — CompleteResearch spent at Start and banked CompletedLevels before the living-army application loop, so an army where every unit sat at the 8-slot EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity ceiling paid for an upgrade nobody received. Implemented the ledger's recorded ruling ("refund the spend when zero units received the modifier"); DW-623 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so the ledger decision was the authority. Change (godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs only): the application loop now counts eligibleUnits alongside DW-83's refusedUnits, and when every eligible unit refused the completion is VOIDED — CompletedLevels rolls back to the pre-completion index, the four Cumulative*Delta totals restore from a snapshot taken BEFORE the accumulate (subtracting the level's delta back off is not an inverse, because SaturatingAdd clamps at the Fixed ceiling), and the level's cost is credited via _resources.Add. The faction still returns to idle so the same level can be re-started at its own cost/time; a voided completion pushes OrderDenied(InventoryFull) — the established modifier-cap denial reason, per ItemSystem's precedent — instead of the ResearchComplete cue, and DW-83's aggregate warn gets a VOIDED+refunded tail. Two guards were added beyond the literal decision text, both to stop the ruling creating a worse defect and both narrowing it: (1) eligibleUnits > 0 — an EMPTY army is not a refusal (the banked level is genuinely received by every future spawn via ApplyCompletedResearch, and a literal "refused == eligible" reading would refund 0 == 0 and make research permanently impossible for an army-less faction, also breaking FutureSpawn_ReceivesCumulativeModifier_ViaApplyCompletedResearch); (2) the cumulative modifier must carry a non-zero payload — a research with no (or net-zero) ResearchModifierDelta is a TECH GATE whose whole value is the banked level PrerequisitesMet reads, so voiding it would break tech unlocks for a starved army. Both have dedicated negative-control tests. Determinism: ResourceStore and ResearchStore are both SimChecksum (v14) inputs, but the new branch is reachable only from a fully-starved army, which no golden scenario builds (ResearchScenario runs one unit with an empty ring) — no golden moved, no re-record, no AlgoVersion/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash touch; the 487-test Golden|Checksum|StartStateHash|CanonicalModelHash filter passed 487/0. Pure sim C# (no using Godot;), Fixed-only (the payload test compares Fixed.Raw, never a float epsilon), ascending-id loop unchanged, no new SoA fields. Tests: 7 new in ResearchSystemTests (void+refund; re-start re-pays the SAME level's cost/time; partial-refusal control; empty-army control; tech-gate control; later-level cumulative rollback proven through a future spawn; saturated-add exact restore) + 1 new in ModifierInstallDiagnosticsTests for the voided warn text; verified red-then-green by reverting ResearchSystem.cs to the run-base version via git show (never git stash) — exactly the 5 positive tests failed, 46/51 — then restored, 51/51. DW-83's existing aggregate-warn test needed one edit (a third unit with ring room, because its two-of-two starved army is now voided rather than banked); it still asserts the same research id / level / "2 living unit(s)" and now also pins that it gets the DW-83 partial tail, not the DW-623 one. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors; suite raw 5177 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (309.68 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 8 new. Follow-ons filed as DW-678 (a zero-payload tech-gate research still burns a ring slot on every unit) and DW-679 (the future-spawn catch-up path still silently drops a banked, paid-for bonus with no refund available).
decision: 2026-08-05 Refund the spend when zero units received the modifier — In CompleteResearch, if the refused count equals the eligible army count (nobody received it), refund _resources.Spend and do not increment CompletedLevels.

### DW-634: A trained worker's rally point is silently overridden by auto-gather on the next tick
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs SpawnTrainedUnit rally branch, vs godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs TickIdle/AssignToNode
severity: low
reason: With the DW-205 residue written, a worker trained from a building that has a rally point still gets CommandState=Move + MoveTarget=rally, but GatheringSystem.TickIdle re-targets MoveTarget to the nearest eligible node on the very next tick, so the rally never takes effect for workers (combat units are unaffected). This matches how a scenario-placed worker behaves and is strictly better than the pre-fix "never gathers, auto-shoots" state, but "walk to the rally point, THEN start gathering" would need a rally-aware first leg or a new gather state. Design question rather than a defect; closure = decide whether worker rally should be honored and, if so, add the first-leg state.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-634 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified against current code as a LIVE defect first: BuildingSystem.SpawnTrainedUnit:360-372 still wrote CommandState=Move + MoveTarget=rally with a NOTE explicitly saying auto-gather wins, and GatheringSystem.TickIdle unconditionally called AssignToNode, overwriting MoveTarget on the next tick. Implemented to the recorded decision plus the owner's MINIMAL-shape scoping note, across 3 source files: (1) EntityWorld gains RallyMovePending — an UNFOLDED one-shot bool[] per-entity flag following the GateClosedTicks/CarryAmount posture (not folded, not persisted, not snapshot residue), with the mandatory Create() recycle-reset and a Clear() entry so the DW-19 reflection sweep stays green; (2) SpawnTrainedUnit's rally branch sets the flag AND EntityFlags.Moving; (3) GatheringSystem.TickIdle stands down while the flag is set, then clears it and runs the UNCHANGED nearest-node logic — so, standing at the rally, the worker picks the mine the player rallied to. No new gather state, no rally-to-resource targeting. Two deliberate scoping calls, both documented in code: (a) arrival uses the PURE-SIM goal test OrderQueueSystem already uses (SqrDistance to CommandGoal vs ArrivalTuning.GoalArriveRadiusSqr), never the presentation-written Moving flag, so headless and live agree, and the gate also releases when any other command state supersedes the rally Move, so an unreachable rally can never park a worker in Idle forever; (b) both new writes are WORKER-ONLY — the rally branch NEVER set EntityFlags.Moving, so no trained unit has ever physically walked to its rally in the sim, and without adding it the new gate would freeze the worker instead of gathering (strictly worse). Setting it for COMBAT units too is the wider correct fix but that path IS golden-covered (ShiftQueueScenario trains a Melee grunt from a rallied Barracks and its recorded checksums encode the grunt standing still), so it belongs in a deliberate re-baseline — filed as DW-680. Determinism: no SimChecksum input changed shape (the new array is unfolded), AlgoVersion untouched, no golden re-recorded, CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash untouched; the only behaviour that moves is a trained WORKER's, a path no golden exercises (no golden trains a Worker-category unit; the only golden that sets a rally trains Melee). Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors; suite Passed 5178 / Failed 0 / Skipped 1 (5170 baseline + 8 new), no flake. Teeth proven: temporarily neutering the TickIdle gate turned 4 of the 7 new tests RED (WithARally_IsNotReTargeted, OnReachingTheRally_GathersFromTheNodeBesideIt, WalksTheWholeRallyLeg_ThenGathersAtTheRalliedMine, RallyPendingWorker_WhoseMoveIsSuperseded), then the gate was restored and the full suite re-ran green. Follow-ons filed as DW-680 (rallied combat units never raise EntityFlags.Moving — golden-blocked) and DW-681 (nothing in the sim layer owns the Move->Stop/Idle transition, which is why the fix needs the one-shot flag rather than reading CommandState).
decision: 2026-08-05 Honor the rally point first, then auto-gather — Add a rally-aware first-leg gather state so TickIdle/AssignToNode does not re-target a worker until it has reached its rally MoveTarget.
scoping-note (owner, 2026-08-05): implement the MINIMAL shape — do NOT build rally-to-resource targeting or a new gather state machine. It is sufficient that the idle-gather sweep stops re-targeting a worker while it still has an outstanding rally MoveTarget. On arrival the worker goes idle and the EXISTING nearest-node logic picks the node next to the rally point, which is the mine the player rallied to. The desired behaviour falls out of the current code once the sweep stops firing too early. Rationale for building at all: an explicit player order must beat automatic behaviour, and the current state means you cannot direct new workers to a specific resource at production time (rallying the town hall to a far mine or a new expansion is standard macro in WC3/SC2/AoE). Note this is sim code and may move Position/SimChecksum — if it does, it joins the golden re-baseline batch.

### DW-636: ScoreBuildSecondBarracks is gated on the SUPPLY expansion, coupling AI production growth to a supply device
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs — ScoreBuildSecondBarracks (`if (!s.HasCCExpansion) return 0f;`)
severity: medium
reason: The AI can only ever build a second Barracks after it has committed the supply-expansion CommandCenter, wiring an economic/production decision to a supply-pressure trigger. That coupling is what forced DW-63's fix to DEPRIORITIZE the ungated expansion (flat 0.25) rather than hard-skip it — a hard skip would permanently cost an ungated-scenario AI its second production building. Closure = decouple the second-Barracks gate onto ore/army demand instead of HasCCExpansion, then revisit whether ScoreExpandSupply can return 0 when gating is disabled. This is a real AI-tuning change with golden implications.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-636 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05), commit 9b89eeea on branch dw/decision-dw-636 atop run-base 01ea6764. Verified LIVE first: AiOpponentSystem.cs still carried `if (!s.HasCCExpansion) return 0f;` in ScoreBuildSecondBarracks, and ScoreExpandSupply still returned the DW-63 EXPAND_SUPPLY_UNGATED = 0.25f. DW-636 does NOT appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger decision line (mirrored verbatim in the worklist bundle intent) was the authority and was followed exactly. Changes, all in godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs: (1) ScoreBuildSecondBarracks re-gated off HasCCExpansion onto ore/army demand — fewer than 2 LIVE Barracks, a COMPLETE first Barracks, an ore surplus past the new SECOND_BARRACKS_ORE_SURPLUS (derived as 2 x COST_BARRACKS so a cost retune moves it), and an available army below the decisive size ScoreLaunchAttack tops its ratio out at (_attackThreshold * 2); the 0.50 score value is UNCHANGED, since the decision replaces the gate, not the tuning weight. AiSnapshot loses HasSecondBarracks/HasCCExpansion and gains LiveBarracksCount + HasOreSurplusForSecondBarracks (the surplus read goes through the same Fixed CanAffordOre comparator as the existing affordability rows — no new float). (2) The "revisit" half of the decision, resolved YES: ScoreExpandSupply now returns a hard 0 when SupplyGatingEnabled is false — DW-63's own comment states it could only deprioritize rather than skip BECAUSE the expansion CC was the second-Barracks gate, and that constraint is gone; the ungated expansion's only remaining payoff is +10 to a cap nothing enforces (DW-637). (3) Collateral defect the decoupling would otherwise have widened: the old first gate read HasSecondBarracks (COMPLETE >= 2), which stays false for the whole time a second Barracks is a construction site, so the AI re-entered the action every tick and stacked duplicate Barracks on the single hardcoded POS_BARRACKS_2 tile for as long as it could afford them; the gate now counts LIVE Barracks. Determinism: NO GOLDEN MOVED AND NONE WAS RE-RECORDED — the recorded decision anticipated an AiActive re-record and it proved unnecessary. AiActiveGoldenTests.MatchesCommittedGolden_OnTheRecordingPlatform passes unmodified, because AiActiveScenario builds its first Barracks on tick 1 with a 10s construction timer and runs exactly 300 ticks = 10s, leaving HasCompleteBarracks false for the entire recording; GoldenScenario/MultiFactionScenario starve Player2 of ore so CanAffordBarracks is false; and the ungated ScoreExpandSupply branch is unreachable for every shipped scenario (none authors a `supply` block, so SupplyConfig.Resolve(null) yields enabled:true). CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash untouched. Coverage: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/AI/AiSecondBarracksDemandTests.cs (7 tests) drives the real AiOpponentSystem.Tick — no reflection, no scorer stub — asserting on the buildings/orders actually committed; verified RED against the pre-fix scorer (4 fail: surplus-driven second Barracks, ungated second Barracks, the fixture-assumption pin, and the rewritten expansion-skip test), and a per-term mutation pass confirmed each of the four gate terms is load-bearing (neutering any one kills exactly one test). DW-63's UngatedSupply_StillCommitsTheExpansion_OnceNothingElseScores was rewritten to the new contract as UngatedSupply_SkipsTheExpansionEntirely (its own docstring already tied its expectation to the coupling this bundle removes), and the behaviour its 0.25 protected is re-pinned by UngatedSupply_StillReachesASecondBarracks_WithoutAnExpansion. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5176 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (278.06 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 7 new - that 1 flake. Follow-ons filed as DW-682 (AI structure placement is five hardcoded tiles with no occupancy/pathability check, now load-bearing far more often) and DW-683 (the second Barracks at 0.50 now outranks the ArcheryRange tech step at 0.49 by a 0.01 float margin).
decision: 2026-08-05 Decouple second-Barracks gate onto ore/army demand — Replace the HasCCExpansion gate in ScoreBuildSecondBarracks with an ore/army-demand score, then revisit whether ScoreExpandSupply can return 0 when gating is disabled; re-record the AiActive golden.

### DW-637: The AI's expansion CommandCenter is neither a resource drop-off nor a production building
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs — DoExpandSupplyCap; godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:245,416
severity: low
reason: DoExpandSupplyCap creates a CommandCenter but never adds it to _productionBuildingIds, and gathering deposits route through the single per-faction ResourceStore.FactionBase rather than the nearest CC — so the expansion's only real payoffs are its +10 SupplyBonus and the second-Barracks unlock (see DW-636). A second base therefore does not behave like an expansion in any economic sense. Closure = make deposits resolve to the nearest owned drop-off and register the expansion for production; this is a design/feature change, not deferred-work repair, so it needs a scoping decision first.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-05 Leave the expansion as supply/unlock only — correct as a burn-down answer, but this entry is MIS-SCOPED and must not be closed here.
reclassify: NOT AI deferred work — this is a missing core mechanic affecting every player. The root cause is not in AiOpponentSystem: gathering deposits route through a single per-faction ResourceStore.FactionBase (GatheringSystem.cs:245,416), so the economy model assumes ONE base per faction. A HUMAN player who builds a second CommandCenter next to a far mine gets the same nothing — no local drop-off, no production. In RTS terms, expansions do not work. Severity 'low' reflects the AI framing and is wrong for the real scope.
gdd-check (2026-08-05): the GDD does NOT explicitly specify multi-base drop-off economy, so this is not a literal unimplemented requirement. BUT the GDD's AI section names `expand` as one of the core scored utility-AI actions ("build workers, expand, attack, research, defend"), which is incoherent if expanding yields only +10 supply — so expansion IS implied as a strategically real act. Treat as a design/roadmap gap requiring its own feature story (drop-off resolution to nearest owned structure, expansion registered for production, rally/control-group implications), NOT a deferred-work repair. Expect Epic 10 live play to surface this loudly on day one.

### DW-642: ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal CREDIT resources on a negative cost - every caller other than the hardened ability path is still exposed

severity: high
reason: This is the primitive behind DW-283: CanAffordOre(faction, -5) is `Ore >= -5`, trivially true, so SpendOre then subtracts a negative and ADDS 5 ore. DW-283 hardened only the ability-cast caller it named; BuildingSystem (train/build/shop), BuyItemCommand, ReviveHeroCommand and AiOpponentSystem share the same primitive and would print resources identically if any of their definitions ever carried a negative cost - and resources are SimChecksum-folded, so an authored negative cost is a money printer, not just a validation gap. The systemic fix is to reject cost < 0 inside SpendOre/SpendCrystal, mirroring ModifierStore.TryDebitEnergy which already refuses it; that is a cross-system change with its own regression surface, which is why it was left out of the ability-cast-path-hardening bundle.

### DW-643: The zero-damage predicate is spelled two different ways and they are complements only by a third system's clamp that the save-restore path bypasses
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:129 (`== Fixed.Zero`) vs godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs:278,312 (`> Fixed.Zero`); clamp at godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:90; unclamped restore at godot/src/Persistence/SaveGameState.cs:649
severity: medium
reason: CombatSystem asks `EffectiveAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero` for non-combatant and AiOpponentSystem asks `> Fixed.Zero` for conscriptable. Those partition the space only because ModifierSystem clamps EffectiveAttackDamage at Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, ...). Paths that write the SoA directly do not go through that clamp - notably SaveGameState's restore, which reconstructs EffectiveAttackDamage from raw ints with no re-clamp. A negative value loaded from a save would then be a COMBATANT to CombatSystem and a NON-combatant to the AI: the two systems would disagree about the same unit. The noncombatant-command-gate bundle deliberately kept both spellings (changing CombatSystem's test to `<=` alters the gate's semantics and risks moving goldens). Closure = one shared predicate, or a clamp on the restore path.
status: open

### DW-644: The AI can pin itself on a raze it is structurally unable to execute - ScoreRazeBuildings counts units DoRazeBuildings then skips for attack domain
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs - ScoreRazeBuildings (~:390) vs DoRazeBuildings (~:515)
severity: medium
reason: Same stall family as DW-202 but the attack-domain half rather than the zero-damage half, and NOT closed by the noncombatant-command-gate bundle's shared IsConscriptable predicate. ScoreRazeBuildings only asks how MANY units are available; DoRazeBuildings then skips every unit whose AttackDomainOf lacks Structure. An AI whose free units are all air-only or anti-unit-only scores RazeBuildings 0.90 every tick and issues zero orders - an indefinite no-op that also starves BuildBarracks (0.85), BuildArcheryRange, BuildSiegeWorkshop and BuildSecondBarracks, all of which score below 0.90, so the AI stops producing entirely. Closure = give the scorer the same Structure-domain term the dispatcher applies, or a fallback when the raze set is empty. Out of that bundle's scope because it changes WHICH action the AI picks - a behaviour change deserving its own golden audit.

So on a DSL-authored victory: (a) GameOverSummary.Build emits a row per faction WITH A LATCHED VERDICT, so the score screen is empty; (b) GameOverPresentation.BuildHeadline keys LocalWin off Verdict[local] == VERDICT_WON, so the player the author just declared the winner is shown the DEFEAT headline alongside a 'Player N Wins!' sub-line (the DW-448 contradiction class at a different surface); (c) OnVictory is bound only by ScenarioDelegateBinder in the Godot scene, so on the dedicated server / headless the leaf does literally nothing and the match never resolves. ### DW-658: BuildingStore.Destroy leaves the razed producer's ProductionQueue slots and ProductionTimer populated - no refund, and phantom orders stay in the checksum fold
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/BuildingStore.cs:355-362 (Destroy) vs godot/src/Core/SimChecksum.cs:406-431 (the fold runs 0..Count with no Alive filter)
severity: medium
reason: Destroy only flips Alive[id] and pushes the free-list entry; the depth-5 queue and head timer are zeroed solely on the next Create of that slot. Two consequences. (1) A producer razed mid-training silently forfeits every paid-for queued order with no refund - WC3 refunds them, and the codebase already has the exact re-resolve-from-def refund machinery in CancelTrainCommand. (2) The dead slot's stale queue bytes and timer stay in the SimChecksum fold until the slot is recycled; deterministic on every peer (Destroy is deterministic and Create zeroes on recycle) so it is not a desync, but the folded state carries phantom orders. Out of the production-queue-correctness bundle's scope: it is a destroy-path refund POLICY decision, not one of the three queue-correctness defects that bundle named, and adding a refund on destroy would move ResourceStore.Ore (a folded value) on a path goldens can reach - it needs its own isolated story. DW-478's QueuedSupply already skips dead buildings explicitly, so the supply reservation is unaffected.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-05 Refund + clear queue at Destroy, re-baseline — In BuildingStore.Destroy, refund the razed producer's queued orders via the CancelTrainCommand re-resolve-from-def path and zero the ProductionQueue slots + ProductionTimer immediately, then re-record the affected SimChecksum goldens.

### DW-664: TickNonCombatant DESTROYS the attack order of a unit whose damage is only TEMPORARILY debuffed to zero
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:253-262 (TickNonCombatant's AttackTarget/AttackBuilding arm), entered from the :155 gate
severity: medium
reason: DW-242 replaced the blanket `if (world.EffectiveAttackDamage[i] == Fixed.Zero) continue;` skip with a route into TickNonCombatant, whose AttackTarget/AttackBuilding arm writes CommandState=Idle, CommandTarget=-1, AttackTarget=-1 and clears Moving|Attacking. Its comment assumes the condition is a permanent authoring property, but the gate reads the EFFECTIVE stat, which ModifierSystem.RecomputeEntity zero-FLOORS (`Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, Fixed.AddSaturating(BaseAttackDamage, _flatAttackDamageBonus))`, ModifierSystem.cs:90) - so any modifier with attack_damage_delta <= -BaseAttackDamage lands a live combatant in that arm. Such content is authorable: Modifier.CheckDelta takes |delta| (Modifier.cs:161) so negative deltas validate, and DW-488 bounds only |delta| x max_stacks. Trigger: force-attack an enemy, then take a temporary attack-damage debuff of at least your base damage; next CombatSystem tick the order is wiped, and on expiry the unit stands Idle instead of resuming - TickIdleCombat re-acquires the NEAREST enemy, not the one the player picked. Pre-DW-242 the bare `continue` mutated nothing, so the order survived the debuff window intact. This also contradicts the disposition the status-flags bundle landed in the same merge range: DW-266 models "cannot attack" as StatusFlags.Disarmed, which CombatSystem.cs:29-31 documents as "still acquires and chases but can never land a hit" (order preserved), and MovementSystem.cs:71-73 states the general rule that a debuff must PAUSE a queued order, not CANCEL it. Two bundles disagree about one situation and the zero-damage path wins because it is tested first. Fix direction: gate the Idle normalization on a PERMANENT non-combatant (BaseAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero) rather than the effective value, so a debuffed combatant keeps its order and resumes on expiry. Not fixed here: it moves live combat behaviour and needs its own golden/checksum judgement, which is a bundle, not a review edit.
status: open

### DW-665: DW-240's fail-closed spawn_unit gate rejects the WHOLE map on a cross-faction skirmish launch
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs:840 (flat trigger channel) and :941-944 (graph channel); the un-remapped source is godot/src/Core/Skirmish/SkirmishSetupToScenario.cs:359
severity: medium
reason: SkirmishSetupToScenario remaps PRE-PLACED unit ids across factions (SkirmishRosterMap.MapUnitId at :143 - alpha's "worker" becomes beta's "forgehand") but copies trigger action unit ids VERBATIM (`UnitId = a.UnitId` at :359), and on the identity-remap path (SkirmishSetupToScenario.cs:161-165) the base triggers are not rewritten at all. DW-240 now hard-fails validation on an unresolvable spawn_unit unit_id. So an authored map whose slot 0 is alpha and which carries a trigger action {"type":"spawn_unit","unit_id":"worker","faction":0}, launched as a skirmish with beta picked for slot 0, resolves IsKnownUnitId("worker", betaDef) = false; ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:65-66 has already written beta into SlotFactionDefs, so Validate fails and :74-76 discards the ENTIRE scenario and boots the flat fallback map. Fix direction: remap the trigger spawn_unit unit_id through SkirmishRosterMap in ReconcileTriggers AND on the identity path (the root cause - the ids are simply wrong for the chosen faction, validator or not); only if that proves impossible should this arm be demoted to a warning.

### DW-666: G is still double-bound after the hotkey-restore pass - grid snap AND the Item Card Editor both fire on one press
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs:537-541 (the `case Key.G:` with no SetInputAsHandled) vs godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:1249-1254; the stale advertisement is MainScene.cs:2032/2037
severity: medium
reason: EntityPlacer._Input's `case Key.G:` toggles grid snap and falls out of the switch WITHOUT calling GetViewport().SetInputAsHandled() - unlike every other branch in that method (Escape :462, Ctrl+Z :483, Delete :499). The event therefore continues to MainScene._UnhandledInput, whose `else if (key.Keycode == Key.G)` calls _ctx.ItemCardPanel.Toggle(). Both handlers are Edit-mode gated, so ONE press of G flips grid snap and simultaneously opens/closes the Item Card Editor. Commit 50f643c was specifically the double-bound-hotkey repair (it rebound K->Ctrl+K and N->Ctrl+N after a58efb4 fixed R) but it missed this pair and then rewrote the hotkey strip to advertise BOTH claimants two lines apart - `G=Snap({snap})` at MainScene.cs:2032 and `G=Item` at MainScene.cs:2037 - so the collision now reads as intended. The same strip line also still advertises `N=Lobby`, which no longer exists: Story 9.7 removed the plain-N lobby bind (see the comment at MainScene.cs:1208-1210) and WaterTool.cs owns plain N, so pressing N toggles the water tool. Every letter A-Z is already claimed in Edit mode, so the fix needs the same modifier treatment 50f643c used (e.g. Ctrl+G for the Item editor, leaving plain G to snap) plus a strip correction - a UI bundle with an in-engine gate, not a review edit.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by the Ctrl-tier keymap policy (7b7713e), NOT by the fix this entry proposes -- and that distinction matters. The entry recommends adding the missing GetViewport().SetInputAsHandled() to EntityPlacer's `case Key.G:`, which would be actively HARMFUL: G is a deliberate BROADCAST key that RegionTool and WaterTool also observe for their own grid-snap (see WaterTool's own status print, 'G grid-snap'), so consuming it in the placer would silently break grid snap in both tools -- trading a double-fire for two dead toggles. The real defect was only that MainScene ALSO opened the Item Card editor on bare G; with every editor moved to Ctrl+<letter> no editor sits on a bare letter at all, so the second consumer is gone by construction and the broadcast stays intact. Verified in-engine from a clean boot: one bare G takes Snap(OFF) -> Snap(ON) with neither the Item nor the DSL Graph editor opening.

### DW-667: Opening the Item Card editor in-engine REWRITES the shipped item JSON — reformats it, reorders keys, drops a zero-valued field and strips the trailing newline

severity: medium

The rewrite is not benign reformatting: `"cost_crystal": 0` is DELETED (consistent with a serializer using WhenWritingDefault), the key order changes (`effect` moves ahead of `cost_ore`), the compact one-line `effect` object is expanded, and the trailing newline is removed. Losing an explicitly-authored zero is a real semantic change for a field a creator may have set deliberately, and the reformat makes every future diff of shipped content noisy. It was caught only because `git status` was checked before committing — an AutoSave or an `git add -A` would have committed corrupted shipped content silently, which is the same class as the Epic-6 AutoSave incident that produced a red baseline for a whole epic. Closure: (a) find why merely opening/binding the panel triggers a write at all (a Save-on-bind or Revalidate-then-persist path); (b) make the writer preserve absent-vs-zero and key order, or make it a targeted JsonNode patch like the FactionWriter precedent (see DW-64's whole-object-replace finding) rather than a full re-serialize; (c) add a Tier-1 round-trip test asserting a shipped item file is byte-identical after a load->save with no edits.

reason: The presence scan applies NO verdict filter, and latched-LOST factions keep their entities on the field by design (class doc: "Eliminated factions' remaining entities/buildings REMAIN in place"). ### DW-687: The DW-620 Invulnerable guard reads a STALE status union on BOTH ModifierStore paths — a collapse during removal is wrongly refused, and a collapse during install is wrongly allowed
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:443-452 (RemoveSlot runs ApplyStatDeltas BEFORE RecomputeStatusUnion) and :186-190 (Apply runs ApplyStatDeltas BEFORE the `StatusFlagsOf |= mod.Status` write), read against the guard at godot/src/Combat/DamageResolver.cs:144
severity: medium
reason: The DW-620 guard puts the flag check inside KillEntity, but both ModifierStore paths mutate stats on one side of the status-union write and therefore hand the guard a flag that does not describe the post-operation host. REMOVE arm (wrongly refused): base MaxHealth 100; install B {id 910, status Invulnerable, max_health_delta +40, duration 60} then A {id 911, max_health_delta -100, permanent} — ceiling 140 then 40, Health clamped to 40. At tick 60 B expires: RemoveSlot -> ApplyStatDeltas(-40) drives the ceiling 40 -> 0, the DW-491 collapse gate is satisfied, KillEntity is REFUSED because StatusFlagsOf still carries the Invulnerable that this very removal is about to clear, and :452 then recomputes the union to None. Final state: alive, EffectiveMaxHealth 0, Health 0, StatusFlags None — the live 0-ceiling zombie DW-325 exists to eliminate, and unreachable by the DW-620 comment's own recovery ("a FRESH collapse once the flag drops") because `ceilingBefore > Fixed.Zero` can never hold again while permanent A is installed; only incoming damage can still kill it, so an unattacked one keeps its faction alive for elimination win conditions indefinitely. APPLY arm (wrongly allowed, the mirror image): a modifier granting Invulnerable together with a net-negative max_health_delta collapses the ceiling at :186 while StatusFlagsOf has not yet been OR-ed at :190, so the modifier KILLS the host it was authored to make death-immune. Distinct from DW-676, which is the definitional pause-vs-cancel question for a host that is GENUINELY immune at collapse time; here the immunity is stale (remove) or not yet installed (apply), and DW-676's deferred-death re-check would not touch the apply arm at all. Uncovered: InvulnerableDeathImmunityTests.CeilingCollapse_KillsTheFormerlyImmuneHost_OnceTheInvulnerabilityExpires expires the -MaxHealth debuff FIRST (duration 1 vs 3), so the hazardous ordering never runs. Latent today — no shipped ability authors a status, so every golden leaves StatusFlagsOf at None — and reachable the moment creator content pairs Invulnerable with a MaxHealth delta. Closure = recompute the status union (or evaluate the guard against the post-operation union) BEFORE the stat revert in RemoveSlot and before the collapse test in Apply, with a two-arm test pinning both orderings.
status: open

### DW-688: The DW-634 rally-arrival test wraps int32 past ~181 units — a long rally reports "arrived" on tick 1 and is silently discarded
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:138 (`FixedVec3.SqrDistance(Position, CommandGoal) <= ArrivalTuning.GoalArriveRadiusSqr`)
severity: medium
reason: Fixed `*` truncates to int32 (`new Fixed((int)(((long)a.Raw * b.Raw) >> 16))`, FixedPoint.cs:69-70), so SqrDistance = Dot(d,d) WRAPS once the squared distance passes 32768, i.e. a separation past ~181 units. At a 250-unit rally leg: Raw 16,384,000 -> ((long)Raw*Raw)>>16 = 4,096,000,000 -> (int) = -198,967,296, and GoalArriveRadiusSqr.Raw is 262,144, so the `<=` compare is TRUE and `arrived` is set on the worker's FIRST idle tick. RallyMovePending clears at :145 and FindBestNode/AssignToNode immediately re-target the worker to the node nearest its SPAWN — exactly the pre-DW-634 behaviour the bundle was chartered to remove, so the fix is a no-op for precisely the long rallies ("rally the hall to a far expansion mine") its own comment cites as motivating. A mid-flight worker walking in from beyond the band is worse than a no-op: at 200u the product is negative too, so it spuriously "arrives" partway and is assigned to whatever node is nearest at that intermediate position. Reachable on every shipped map (ScenarioData.MapBounds defaults to 120, MapSize.Large is a 128 half-extent = a 256-unit span). Int32 wrap is well-defined in C# so every peer computes the same wrong answer (no lockstep divergence), but the state it drives — GatherTarget, MoveTarget, and ResourceNodeStore.AssignedGatherers, which IS folded into SimChecksum — is sim truth, so this is a wrong-but-deterministic sim outcome, not a cosmetic one. HeroXpSystem.cs:96-109 documents this exact overflow and works around it with long-widened raws; the new call site does not. Unpinned: TrainedWorkerRallyFirstLegTests rallies to (22,0), a 22-unit leg. Same unwidened pattern is pre-existing at OrderQueueSystem.cs:74 and CombatSystem.cs:514/:622 against the same 2u radius, so a fix should cover the shared arrival predicate rather than this one line. Closure = a long-widened squared-distance helper (the HeroXpSystem pattern) used by every ArrivalTuning goal test, with a test at a >181-unit leg.
status: open

### DW-689: An UNREACHABLE rally point parks a trained worker in Idle permanently — the DW-634 gate's "superseded" escape cannot fire in the sim layer
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:133-146 (the RallyMovePending stand-down; the escape at :144 is `CommandState != UnitCommand.Move`)
severity: medium
reason: The stand-down clears RallyMovePending only on arrival within GoalArriveRadiusSqr, or when CommandState leaves Move — and nothing in the SIMULATION layer ever takes a rallied worker out of Move. CombatSystem.cs:136-147's gatherer normalization rewrites AttackMove/Stop/HoldPosition/AttackTarget/Patrol/Follow/PatrolAppend/AttackBuilding to Idle but NOT Move, then `continue`s past every other Idle write in that file; OrderQueueSystem skips an entity with an empty queue (a freshly trained worker has one); BuildingSystem.ClearWorkerBuild fires only from CommandState=Build; the only Move->Stop writers are PathRequestSystem.cs:190/:234 and FlowFieldBridge.cs:172, all under src/UI (presentation, absent headless) and all gated on WAYPOINT_REACH_SQR (1.5u), strictly tighter than the 2u arrival test on :138, so they can never fire where :144 has not already passed. Trigger: an authored Custom building with produces_category "Worker" (the only worker producer TrainUnit accepts) rallied to a point inside a PathabilityGrid-blocked region — MovementSystem.cs:195-206 hard-stops the worker at the blocked-cell boundary, so SqrDistance(Position, CommandGoal) never falls inside the radius and TickIdle returns at :144 on every tick forever. FindBestNode/AssignToNode are never reached: the worker never gathers again, a silent permanent loss of its economic function, where pre-DW-634 it was re-targeted to the nearest node on the very next tick. The bundle's own comment at :140-143 claims to prevent exactly this, and its escape test (TrainedWorkerRallyFirstLegTests.RallyPendingWorker_WhoseMoveIsSuperseded_ResumesAutoGatherWithoutReachingTheRally) hand-writes CommandState = Idle, a value the simulation never assigns to this unit on its own. Related but NOT covered by DW-681 (which records the layering gap; its closure — move goal-arrival resolution into a sim system — still only fires ON arrival) or DW-682 (AI placement). Closure = a bounded stand-down (a tick budget or a reachability/no-progress test) that releases the worker to auto-gather when the rally leg provably cannot complete.
status: open

### DW-690: RallyMovePending is the one input to its own gate that SaveGameState drops, so a save/load mid-rally reverts the DW-634 fix — and the comment justifying the omission is factually wrong
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/EntityWorld.cs:681-687 (the "not persisted" rationale) vs godot/src/Core/Persistence/SaveGameState.cs:167 (the EA enum), :266-267/:290-291 (capture), :636/:664-665 (restore)
severity: low
reason: SaveGameState round-trips Flags, CommandState, MoveTarget, CommandGoal, GatherState, GatherTarget, CarryAmount, CarryResType, CarryCapacity and BuildTarget, but RallyMovePending is not in the EA enum and comes back false from EntityWorld.Create. A worker autosaved mid-leg therefore reloads looking exactly like it is still walking the rally (Flags/CommandState/MoveTarget all restored) while its gate is off, so the first GatheringSystem tick runs FindBestNode/AssignToNode and overwrites MoveTarget with whatever node is nearest its mid-leg position — the player's explicit rally discarded, the precise defect DW-634 was chartered to fix. The EntityWorld doc defends the omission as "the exact posture of every other field of this worker state machine (GatherState/GatherTarget/CarryAmount/GateClosedTicks are all unfolded)", which conflates UNFOLDED with UNPERSISTED: three of those four ARE persisted and only GateClosedTicks is genuinely absent from EA, so the stated rationale does not hold even though the omission may still be the right call. Closure = either add RallyMovePending to the EA enum/capture/restore (a save-format addition, no fold and no golden movement) or correct the comment to state the real reason for dropping an in-flight rally leg across a load.
status: open

### DW-691: The DeathFeed is unthreaded on every EFFECT-GRAPH EffectContext — a hero that lands the last hit through a modifier period or an on-hit rider gains no XP
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:839 (RunEffect builds its EffectContext with the `deaths` parameter omitted; the store has no DeathFeed field at all — fields :76-86, ctor :100-108) and godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:830-833 (RunOnHit, same omission); godot/src/Combat/ItemSystem.cs:236-237 likewise
severity: medium
reason: EffectContext defaults `deaths` to null (EffectContext.cs:71-75), so a DamageEffect leaf reached through a modifier's period_effect, through an on-hit rider, or through a consumable's graph calls DamageResolver.Apply with ctx.Deaths null and the `deaths?.Push(...)` at DamageResolver.cs:161 no-ops. HeroXpSystem.Tick reads only that feed (:83-86), so a hero whose poison DoT or whose on-hit rider lands the killing blow banks 0 XP, while the identical last hit from its auto-attack credits world.XpBounty in full — the three cast contexts in AbilityCastSystem (:200-202, :269-271, :417-419) and ScenarioDirector (:2824-2826) all DO pass `deaths`, so this is an inconsistency between sibling effect paths, not a design stance. Shipped content already reaches one arm: onhit_searing.json carries a damage leaf and runs through the CombatSystem context. HeroStore Xp/Level are folded into SimChecksum, so the withheld credit is folded state, which makes DW-616's new DeathFeed class doc ("a death is NEVER dropped", DeathFeed.cs:37-40) true only of the feed's CAPACITY, not of the channel — DW-616 closed a loss needing >256 deaths in one tick while these paths withhold XP in ordinary play. Scoped to the effect-graph contexts: DW-490 already covers the sibling omission on the DW-325 ceiling-collapse KillEntity call (ModifierStore.cs:766), which also needs a caster-attribution decision this entry does not. Closure = thread the DeathFeed into ModifierStore (a ctor dep, like _events/_stats) and into RunOnHit/UseItemCommand, then re-check the DW-616 invariant statement.
status: open
